S03: Tobias and Ivy meet at a beach party in a seaside town at the end of the rail line and break into an empty house on the shore.
They fall in love - the ice on the frozen river, the noodle house, the drive-in.
The relationship curdles into recrimination over Ivy's drinking and Tobias's withholding.
Ivy comes home drunk having dented Tobias's car, and the fight ends with her walking out for good.
Ivy hires a memory-erasure clinic to remove every trace of Tobias from her mind.
Tobias visits the bookshop and finds Ivy treating him as a stranger and flirting with a young man named Peck.
Nina and Grady show Tobias the form letter from the clinic, and he goes to its director, Dr. Hallam, demanding the same procedure.
Tobias boxes up every object connected with Ivy so that the clinic can map the memories attached to them.
The technicians Dell and Peck run the erasure in Tobias's flat, and Peck pockets the mementos to use on Ivy.
Inside his own head Tobias watches the most recent and ugliest memories dissolve around him one by one.
Reaching the memories he loves, Tobias changes his mind and tries to smuggle Ivy into memories she was never part of.
Dell and the receptionist Rosa get high on Tobias's bed and lose track of the procedure as his map goes off the rails.
Dr. Hallam arrives to re-map the erasure, and Rosa kisses him - only for his wife to reveal that Rosa's own affair with him was erased.
In the last surviving memory, the empty house on the shore, Tobias and Ivy say goodbye and she tells him to meet her at the beach.
The erasure completes and Tobias wakes with no memory that Ivy ever existed.
Tobias skips work on an impulse he cannot account for, takes the train to the coast and meets Ivy on the frozen sand.
They drive back to the city together and she invites him up to her flat.
Rosa quits the clinic and mails the files and session tapes back to every patient on the books.
Tobias and Ivy listen to their own recorded voices tearing each other apart; she runs, comes back, and they agree to try anyway.
S02: Insurance investigator Martin Kray interviews a claimant named Elias Prine and rules his memory loss psychosomatic, denying the claim.
Elias's diabetic wife tests him by asking for injection after injection, and dies of the overdose he cannot remember giving her.
Intruders attack Martin and his wife in their bathroom; Martin kills one and is struck in the head, losing the ability to form new memories.
Martin builds a system of instant photographs, annotated notes and tattoos to hunt the second attacker, a man he knows only by the initials R.M.
A plainclothes officer called Roy helps Martin find and kill the real attacker, a killing Martin forgets within minutes.
In a motel room he cannot remember checking into, Martin narrates the Prine case down the phone to an anonymous caller.
Martin burns his wife's hairbrush and books in a field, trying to grieve a loss he can never retain.
The caller feeds Martin a name and a location, identifying the drug dealer Gil Marsh as the man he is looking for.
Martin beats and strangles Gil in a derelict basement and photographs the body.
As he dies Gil whispers "Elias", which Martin cannot explain, and Martin changes into the dead man's suit and takes his sports car.
Roy arrives and tells Martin that Gil was innocent, that Martin avenged his wife, and that Martin is himself the man in the Prine story.
Rather than believe him, Martin burns the photographs of Gil, writes "he is lying to you" on Roy's picture and copies down Roy's licence plate as his next target.
Martin drives to a tattoo parlour and has the plate inked on his thigh as the sixth fact.
At her bar, Gil's girlfriend Corinne recognises the dead man's clothes and car and serves Martin a beer the staff have spat in.
Corinne hides every pen in her house, goads Martin into hitting her, then returns bruised and blames a man called Vance so that Martin will go after him.
Martin ambushes Vance in a motel bathroom, beats him and drives him out of town at gunpoint.
Corinne runs the licence plate through a friend at the vehicle registry and hands Martin a record naming Roy Mercer.
Martin lures Roy to the derelict building, shoots him in the head and photographs the corpse.
S04: In a hill village in the old country, the local strongman Peppino has Emilio Nardi's father and brother killed and sends his men after the boy.
Emilio's mother is shot dead bargaining for his life, and the boy is smuggled overseas and renamed Emilio Rocca at the immigration station.
In the immigrant quarter, Emilio loses his grocery job when the extortionist Serafino forces the owner to hire his nephew instead.
Bruno draws Emilio into hiding a cache of guns and then into stealing a rug, beginning their partnership.
Serafino demands a cut of the young men's take, and Emilio persuades Bruno and Aldo to let him handle it his own way.
During the neighbourhood festival Emilio shoots Serafino dead on his own staircase and quietly assumes his place as the local protector.
Emilio builds an olive oil importing company and settles neighbourhood grievances, forcing an old widow's landlord to back down.
Emilio sails back to the old country and guts Peppino with a knife, closing the vendetta.
The family gathers to surprise Emilio on his birthday, and his youngest son Dante announces he has enlisted in the infantry.
At the lake house, Dante conducts business through his son's first communion party while his sister Rosa asks leave to marry a man named Wynn.
Franco Ventresca complains that the Fossi brothers, protected by Aaron Held, are taking his city territory.
Gunmen fire into Dante and Claire's bedroom, and Dante concludes the order came from inside his own house.
Dante tells Held in the south and Ventresca in the city that he blames the other, setting the two men against each other.
The Fossis garrotte Ventresca in a bar and flee when a policeman walks in, leaving him alive.
In the island capital, Dante watches Held's partners carve up the country and has Held's man Nico Ferra strangled in his hotel room.
Dante's brother Sandro lets slip that he knew Ferra, and Dante kisses him and disowns him as the island's government collapses around them.
Home again, Dante learns Claire has lost the baby and that Ventresca survived and is talking to federal agents.
At the legislative hearing Ventresca recants his testimony when Dante seats his brother from the old country in the gallery behind him.
Claire tells Dante the miscarriage was an abortion and that she is leaving; he strikes her and keeps the children.
After their mother's funeral Dante has Held shot at an airport, Ventresca persuaded to open his veins, and Sandro shot on the lake.
S01: A returning prisoner of war delivers to a young boy the gold watch his father kept hidden through years of captivity.
Hitmen Rollo and Marcus drive across the city debating foreign drug laws and what fast food is called abroad.
Waiting in the corridor outside their target's flat, the two argue over whether a foot massage is worth killing a man for.
Marcus recites a passage of scripture and the pair shoot a young man named Tobin for double-crossing their employer, Otis, and recover a briefcase.
A fourth man hidden in the bathroom empties a revolver at them without hitting either, which Marcus calls divine intervention.
In the car Rollo's gun goes off and blows the head off their passenger Del.
Marcus parks the bloodied car at his friend Warren's house, where a fixer directs the cleanup and gives the men fresh clothes.
Over breakfast in a coffee shop, two small-time robbers decide on the spot to hold up the diner they are sitting in.
Marcus talks the robber down mid-holdup, hands over his own wallet, keeps the briefcase and lets the couple walk out.
The two hitmen deliver the briefcase to Otis at his bar, where Otis is paying the ageing boxer Denny to take a dive in the fifth.
Rollo buys heroin from his dealer Kip and shoots up before his night out.
Rollo takes Otis's wife Nadia to a themed diner where they win the dance contest.
Nadia snorts Rollo's heroin, overdoses, and is revived by an adrenaline shot to the heart on the dealer's living-room floor.
Denny double-crosses Otis, wins the fight and kills his opponent in the ring, then escapes in a taxi.
Hiding in a motel with his girlfriend Marielle, Denny discovers she has left his father's watch behind in his flat.
Denny returns for the watch and shoots Rollo dead with a submachine gun left on the kitchen counter.
Denny and Otis collide in the street, crash, and are taken prisoner in the basement of a pawnshop.
Denny breaks free, comes back with a sword from the shop wall while one of their captors is raping Otis, and Otis declares them square on condition Denny leaves town.
Denny collects Marielle and rides out of the city on a motorcycle taken from the pawnshop.
S06: Undercover officer Danny Roarke rehearses a fabricated anecdote about a drug bust in a public toilet with his handler Pruitt until he can tell it like a memory.
Danny performs the anecdote for the boss Bram, his son Cal and Mr. Ash, and is taken onto the crew as Mr. Elm.
Ren Vasco walks out of prison and reports to Bram and Cal, who owe him for keeping his mouth shut.
Over breakfast the crew argue about what a pop song is really about and whether waitresses deserve a tip.
Bram hands out the tree aliases and Mr. Birch objects to being Mr. Birch.
The robbery collapses within a minute, and Mr. Ash shoots his way clear of the police from the getaway car with Mr. Elm beside him.
Fleeing on foot, Mr. Elm hijacks a car and is shot in the stomach by the terrified driver, whom he shoots dead.
Mr. Ash drives the screaming Elm to the warehouse rendezvous, cradles him and swears he is not going to die.
Mr. Birch arrives, argues that the job was a setup with an informer inside it, and hides the diamonds outside the building.
Mr. Cedar strolls in and produces a kidnapped patrolman, Doyle, from the boot of his car.
Left alone with the bound officer, Mr. Cedar dances to a radio oldie, cuts off his ear and douses him in petrol.
Mr. Elm shoots Mr. Cedar dead from the floor and tells Doyle that he is a cop and that the police are waiting outside for Bram.
Cal returns, listens to Elm's account of Cedar, and shoots Doyle dead himself.
Bram arrives, names Mr. Elm as the informer, and Mr. Ash refuses to believe him and turns his gun on Bram.
The three-way standoff leaves Bram, Cal and Ash all shot, with only Ash and Elm still breathing.
Elm confesses that he is a police officer, Ash shoots him as the police storm the warehouse, and Ash is cut down.
S07: Mathematician Aaron Vale is told that his failing heart will kill him unless a donor is found.
His estranged wife Della presses him to agree to be inseminated with his frozen sperm before he dies.
Ex-convict Wes Tarrow, born again, holds down a job and coaches boys' baseball while his wife Nita dreads his fanaticism and his temper.
Lena Ward, a recovered addict, lives a settled suburban life with her husband Doug and their two young daughters.
Wes's pickup hits Doug and both girls at a crossing; he drives off, turns back, and then flees.
Lena is told at the hospital that her husband and both children are dead.
Doug's heart is transplanted into Aaron, who wakes up alive.
Wes walks into a police station, confesses to the hit-and-run and is sent back to prison.
Lena goes back to cocaine and begins methodically destroying herself.
Unable to stop thinking about whose heart is beating in his chest, Aaron hires a private investigator to find the donor's widow.
Aaron follows Lena, engineers a meeting at a swimming pool, and the two begin an affair.
Aaron leaves Della and tells her he does not want the child she is trying to conceive.
Aaron admits to Lena that he is carrying her husband's heart; she throws him out, then takes him back.
Released early, Wes walks out on Nita and on his faith and takes work at a motel far from home.
Lena demands that Wes be killed, and Aaron buys a gun and tracks him to the motel.
Aaron cannot go through with it and only wounds Wes, telling him to run.
Wes follows the pair back to their motel and asks Aaron to finish the job, and Aaron turns the gun on himself instead.
Lena and Wes get the dying Aaron to a hospital where the transplanted heart fails; Wes goes home to his family and Lena, pregnant, goes home alone.
S08: In a city in the east, the deaf teenager Suki is the one who finds her mother dead after she takes her own life.
On a hunting trip in a desert country, the businessman Ken Arata makes a gift of his rifle to his guide Rashid.
Rashid sells the rifle on to the goatherd Nasser, who needs it for the jackals taking his flock.
Nasser hands the rifle to his sons Idris and Tarek and sends them into the hills with the goats.
The boys argue about how far the rifle will carry, and Tarek fires at a distant tourist bus to settle it.
Foreign tourists Alan and Ruth Craven, travelling to repair a marriage broken by the cot death of their baby, are on that bus.
The bullet goes through Ruth's shoulder and the bus turns off for a mountain village.
Alan begs his embassy for a helicopter while a village vet stitches Ruth and the other tourists grow mutinous and drive away.
Back home, the Cravens' nanny Rosalva, unable to find anyone to cover for her, takes Ben and Lily across the border to her son's wedding.
Suki is humiliated at a volleyball match and brushed off by boys in a restaurant because she cannot speak.
Suki takes off her underwear at the table and exposes herself to her dentist, hunting for any reaction at all.
Police trace the rifle back to Rashid and beat his family until he names Nasser.
A helicopter lifts Ruth out to a hospital in the capital.
Rosalva's nephew Beto drives the children back drunk, panics at the border checkpoint and abandons the three of them in the desert.
Rosalva walks into the desert with the children, leaves them under a tree to find help, and is arrested by the border patrol.
Police corner Nasser's family in the rocks; Idris is shot dead and Tarek surrenders, confessing that he fired the shot.
Rosalva is deported after sixteen years in the country, though the children are found alive.
A detective named Sano tells Suki that the police only wanted to confirm what became of the rifle her father legally gave away.
Suki meets Sano naked at her door, weeps in his arms and hands him a folded note.
Ken Arata comes home and holds his daughter on the balcony high above the city.
S10: Ruben shares a cramped house with his mother, his brother Nestor, Nestor's wife Alma and their baby.
Nestor robs a pharmacy and beats Alma at home, and Ruben begins pressing her to run away with him.
Ruben discovers that Nestor's rottweiler Tigre kills other dogs on sight and starts entering him in the local dogfights, winning steadily.
Ruben pays two thugs to beat Nestor, who responds by taking Alma, the baby and Ruben's hidden savings and disappearing.
Model Celine Vaz's lover Hector walks out on his wife and daughters and moves her into a new flat facing her own billboard.
In a fight the promoter Chaco shoots Tigre in the ring, Ruben stabs him and flees with his friend Pipo.
Ruben runs a red light at speed and ploughs into Celine's car.
Cardo, a former guerrilla turned vagrant contract killer, is at the junction and drags the bleeding Tigre out of the wreck.
Celine wakes in hospital with her leg pinned together and her lapdog Chispa lost somewhere in the new flat.
Chispa falls through a hole in the floorboards, and Hector tears up the floor while Celine's leg turns gangrenous.
Celine's leg is amputated and the billboard carrying her image is taken down.
Nestor is shot dead robbing a bank, and at the funeral Alma refuses Ruben's offer to leave with him.
Cardo nurses Tigre back to health among his own pack of strays.
The businessman Elian hires Cardo to murder his half-brother and business partner Sergio.
Cardo watches from a distance as his estranged wife is buried, then follows his grown daughter Perla home.
Tigre kills every other dog in Cardo's yard while he is out, and Cardo puts a gun to the dog's head and cannot fire.
Cardo abducts Sergio but chains him up in his lair instead of killing him.
Cardo brings Elian face to face with his brother, leaves a loaded pistol between them, and walks out having taken money from both.
Cardo breaks into Perla's flat, leaves a long confession of who he is on her answering machine and takes her photograph.
Shaved and in clean clothes, Cardo leaves his money for Perla and walks out into the wasteland with Tigre.
S09: An immigrant shopkeeper named Nadir and his daughter Sahar buy a handgun while the dealer mocks the way he speaks.
Trey and Kwame carjack the prosecutor Halstead's car outside a restaurant.
Officer Boyle pulls over the Hobarts, gropes Renee in front of her husband Clay, and lets them go with a warning.
Boyle's partner Voss asks their commander for a new patrol car rather than keep riding with a racist.
Locksmith Mateo changes the Halsteads' locks while Paula loudly assumes he is a gang member about to sell her keys.
Mateo replaces the lock on Nadir's shop and warns him the door itself is broken, and Nadir accuses him of running a con.
Boyle pleads with a health insurance clerk, Delia Frank, for treatment for his father and is refused.
Nadir's shop is smashed and looted, and the insurer refuses to pay because he ignored the warning about the door.
Renee is trapped upside down in a burning wreck and Boyle, the officer who assaulted her, crawls in and drags her out.
Trey and Kwame run down a shopkeeper named Pham and dump him outside a hospital.
Clay is stopped mid-carjacking of his own car and Voss talks the other officers out of shooting him.
Clay drives Trey away from the police at speed and then throws him out of the car.
Nadir waits outside Mateo's house with the gun and fires just as Mateo's small daughter Rosie runs into his arms.
The child is untouched - Sahar had bought blanks - and Nadir decides she is his angel.
Voss picks up Kwame hitchhiking, misreads him reaching into his pocket, shoots him dead and burns the car.
Detective Isaiah Reece is called to a body dumped by the roadside and finds that it is his brother Kwame.
Reece's mother blames him for never going to look for his brother.
Paula falls down her stairs and tells her housekeeper Alba that she is the only friend she has.
Trey finds Pham's van packed with trafficked migrants and turns them loose at the docks instead of selling them.
A collision starts an argument in the street.
S12: An insomniac product-recall investigator finds that the only thing that lets him sleep is crying at support groups for diseases he does not have.
Ada Vey starts attending the same groups, and her obvious faking destroys his release.
On a business flight the narrator meets soap salesman Rex Marrow and pockets his card.
The narrator's flat and all his catalogue furniture are destroyed in an explosion, and he calls Rex, who takes him into a derelict house at the edge of the industrial district.
Outside a bar Rex asks the narrator to hit him as hard as he can, and the two beat each other bloody in the car park.
What starts as two men brawling hardens into a basement club with its own rules, pulling in more and more members.
Ada overdoses, Rex brings her back to the derelict house, and the two begin a loud affair the narrator cannot stand.
Rex renders fat stolen from a cosmetic surgery clinic into soap and sells it back to the department stores at eighty dollars a bar.
Rex burns the narrator's hand with lye and holds him there, refusing to let him retreat into meditation.
The narrator blackmails his employer into paying him to stay away, using his own beaten face as the evidence.
Rex turns the club into an organisation he calls Havoc, filling the house with shaven recruits who take orders and vandalise corporate property.
Rex steers the car into oncoming traffic, lets it roll, and then disappears.
A member of Havoc named Ogden is shot dead on an operation, and the narrator starts trying to shut the whole thing down.
Travelling city to city, the narrator finds identical clubs everywhere and men who greet him as Rex Marrow.
The narrator works out that he and Rex are the same person, and that Rex has been acting while he sleeps.
Ada confirms that she has been sleeping with him, not with a separate man.
The narrator discovers that Havoc has mined the towers of the debt-record companies and tries to defuse the charges.
Rex beats him down a stairwell in one of the towers, and the narrator puts a gun in his own mouth and shoots himself through the cheek to kill Rex.
Ada is delivered to the tower by the shaven recruits, and the two hold hands at the window as the buildings come down.
S13: Lise lies in bed with Cort describing a recurring dream of a red tunnel while the two tease each other about her ex-boyfriend Jonah.
Alone in the flat, Lise takes a pregnancy test and finds that it is positive.
Lise reads in a park among sprinklers and playing children, one hand resting on her stomach.
Lise, Cort and Jonah ride the underground to a party, arguing cheerfully about sex and about Cort's drinking.
At the party Cort gets steadily drunk and high and starts pursuing other women, and a disgusted Lise leaves on her own.
Rather than cross a busy road Lise takes a pedestrian underpass and walks in on a pimp known as the Adder beating a transsexual woman.
The Adder rapes Lise and beats her head against the concrete while a passer-by glimpses them and backs away.
Cort and Jonah come out of the party to find Lise being loaded into an ambulance.
Two men in the street offer to sell Cort the rapist's name and steer him and Jonah towards a club called the Pit.
Cort hunts through the club, seizes the wrong man and has his arm snapped.
Jonah beats that man's face in with a fire extinguisher while the real Adder watches from a few feet away.
Police handcuff Cort and Jonah and carry the pair out of the club into the street.
In a flat overlooking that street, an old man is explaining to a younger one that nothing survives time.
S11: In a far country, gangsters hold the family of a criminal known as Varga hostage, and he kills his own wife and children and then everyone connected to the men, and disappears into legend.
Five criminals - Deane, Corbin, Lasko, Riis and Willem Kade - are pulled into a hijacking lineup and held in the same cell.
In the cell they plan revenge on a police escort racket, a ring of corrupt officers moving smugglers across the city.
The crew ambush the escort, and the ensuing scandal tears the department apart.
Deane's lawyer and lover Rhea Dolan gets them out to the coast, where Corbin's contact Whit buys the stolen jewels.
Whit puts them on to a jeweller who turns out to be a courier carrying heroin, and the crew realise they are being steered.
A lawyer named Vasiliev appears, says he acts for Varga, tells each man he has unknowingly stolen from Varga, and orders them to destroy a boatload of his rivals' cocaine.
Lasko runs and is found shot dead on a beach.
The crew try to kill Vasiliev in his office and back off when he reveals he is holding Rhea.
The four survivors board the rival's boat in the harbour.
Riis and Corbin are killed below decks, and there is no cocaine anywhere on the ship.
Deane is shot by a figure on deck while Kade watches from the dockside, and the boat goes up in flames.
An investigator named Dagg questions Kade in a borrowed police office by the harbour, pressing him to give up Deane.
A burned survivor tells investigators from his hospital bed that Varga was on the boat, and begins describing him to a sketch artist.
Kade, granted immunity, tells Dagg that Deane was Varga, collects his belongings and walks out of the station.
Dagg realises that Kade improvised the entire story from the noticeboard behind the desk and the maker's name on the bottom of a coffee cup.
Kade's limp and his crippled hand straighten out as he walks down the street, and Vasiliev collects him in a waiting car.
The faxed sketch finishes printing, and the face on it is Kade's.
S15: Twelve alien vessels appear at points around the planet and the world's militaries mobilise.
An officer named Braid recruits linguist Marion Ashe to translate the visitors' language at the northern plains site.
Marion and physicist Cole Reddick enter the shell and make contact through the barrier with the two creatures they nickname Pike and Perch.
Marion takes off her hazmat suit to show the visitors a human face, and the two sides begin building a vocabulary out of circular written marks.
As Marion learns the circular language she has vivid, unplaceable visions of a daughter.
The twelve sites share their findings until one government's translation of the phrase "offer weapon" fractures the coalition and the exchanges stop.
Rogue soldiers plant a bomb inside the shell while Marion and Cole are working in it.
Pike shields the two humans from the blast and is fatally injured, and the shell withdraws out of reach.
Governments pull out one by one, an ultimatum is issued, and the camp is ordered to evacuate.
Marion is lifted alone into the shell, where Perch explains that the weapon is the language itself and that the visitors have come because they will need humanity's help.
Marion understands that learning the language has unmoored her from linear time and that her visions are memories of a future.
In one such vision Marion sees herself at an international gala being thanked in private by a commander named Wen.
Using what the vision showed her, Marion phones Wen's private number and recites his dying wife's words, and he stands down his fleet.
The other governments follow, the coalition re-forms, and the twelve shells rise and vanish.
Cole tells Marion he is amazed by her, and she chooses to have the child with him knowing exactly how it will end.
Marion and Cole's daughter Nella is born and grows up, and Marion plays with her and teaches her words.
Nella is diagnosed with an incurable illness, and Marion tells her that her father walked out after she told him something he could not accept.
Nella dies in hospital with Marion holding her.
S16: Renn and his wife Isa spend fifty subjective years together on the deep level, building a world out of memory.
To get Isa to wake up, Renn plants in her mind the idea that her world is not real.
The idea keeps growing, and Isa throws herself from a hotel window and frames Renn for her murder.
Renn flees the country and works as an extractor for hire, unable to go home to his children.
Renn and Dax run an extraction on the energy magnate Halvard that collapses when Isa's projection intervenes.
Halvard, impressed rather than angry, hires Renn to plant an idea in his rival's heir Theo Brandt in exchange for having his record cleared.
Renn assembles the chemist Sabir, the forger Quill and the student architect Sable, whom his father-in-law Hoyt points him to at the university.
Sable learns to build dream architecture and finds the memory prison in Renn's mind where the projection of Isa lives.
Theo's father dies and the team books the son onto a ten-hour flight home.
On the first level Sabir drives the van through rain-soaked streets while Theo's militarised subconscious attacks and Halvard is shot.
On the second level Quill impersonates Theo's godfather Crale in a hotel to turn Theo against him.
On the third level the team assault a snow fortress where Quill sets charges and Theo is meant to reach his father's safe.
Isa's projection shoots Theo dead inside the fortress, and Renn and Sable go down to the deep level to bring him back.
Renn admits to the projection that he was the one who planted the idea that killed his wife.
Renn refuses the projection's offer to stay and lets her go.
Sable pushes Theo off a balcony to wake him, and he opens his father's safe to find the will and the paper pinwheel.
Sabir's van hits the water, Dax's lift charge fires and Quill blows the fortress, and the jolts cascade back up through the levels.
Renn stays behind on the deep level to search for the aged Halvard.
Renn washes up on a shore and is carried to a castle where Halvard is an old man, and the two remind each other of their bargain and shoot themselves awake.
Everyone wakes on the plane, Halvard makes the phone call, Renn is waved through immigration and comes home to his children as the spinning top wobbles on the table.
S19: As shills, Julian Croft and Silas Roe plant themselves in the audience for the conjuror Prosper, with Julian's wife Vesna performing the water-tank escape.
Silas ties the wrong knot before the escape and Vesna drowns in front of the audience.
Julian blames Silas, and their feud costs Silas two fingers when Julian sabotages his bullet catch.
Silas debuts an illusion he calls The Vanishing Act, stepping into one cabinet and out of another across the stage in an instant.
Julian hires a drunk lookalike to reproduce the trick, and Silas wrecks the act by taking the double's place beneath the stage.
Julian sends his assistant Ines to spy on Silas, and she falls in love with him instead.
Ines brings Julian the coded diary, and Silas supplies the keyword knowing she will pass it on.
The diary sends Julian across the country to a mountain town to find the reclusive inventor Kessler.
Kessler builds Julian a machine that does not transport but duplicates, and Julian tests it on his hat and on a cat.
Kessler is driven out of the town and leaves the machine behind with a written warning to drown it in the sea.
Julian stages his own version of the illusion, drowning the copy left under the stage at every single performance.
Silas sneaks beneath the stage and watches Julian drown in a locked water tank.
Silas is convicted of Julian's murder, held in gaol reading Julian's diary, and stripped of custody of his daughter.
A collector calling himself Aylward, who is Julian alive and in disguise, buys Silas's secrets and takes the child.
The stage manager Braddock delivers the machine to Aylward's theatre and realises who Aylward really is.
Silas's twin, who has shared his name and his life, shoots Julian in the theatre and takes his daughter back.
Julian dies on the floor among the tanks holding every copy of himself he has drowned.
S20: A travelling priest passes the soldier Davin and his veiled wife Sela on the forest road.
The bandit Korrin, dozing under a tree, watches them go by and glimpses Sela's face when the breeze lifts her veil.
Korrin lures Davin off the path with a story of buried swords and ties him to a tree.
Korrin brings Sela to the clearing and forces himself on her while her bound husband watches.
Sela demands that the two men fight to decide which of them she belongs to.
Korrin cuts Davin's bonds and the two fight clumsily and in open terror.
Davin is killed and Sela runs from the thicket.
Korrin takes the soldier's sword and horse and leaves.
A woodcutter stumbles on the body in the undergrowth, runs off to report it, and quietly takes the costly dagger with him.
A constable captures Korrin by the river after the stolen horse throws him.
At the court Korrin boasts that he killed the soldier in a magnificent duel of nineteen strokes.
At a temple Sela testifies that her husband looked at her with contempt, and that she fainted holding her dagger and woke to find it in his chest.
Speaking through a medium, the dead Davin says his wife asked the bandit to kill him, and that he took his own life with the dagger in his shame.
Sheltering from the rain under a ruined gate, the woodcutter and the priest tell a passing stranger that they cannot make sense of what they heard.
The woodcutter admits he saw the whole thing and describes a squalid, cowardly fight in which both men begged and the soldier died almost by accident.
The stranger points out that the woodcutter stole the dagger, which is why he lied to the court.
An abandoned baby is found under the gate and the stranger strips it of its clothes.
The woodcutter carries the baby home to raise with his own six, and the priest's faith in people comes back.
S21: In the shanties, Aarav and Vikas Sethi play cricket on an airstrip and are chased off it.
Aarav drops through a latrine pit to reach the country's biggest film star for an autograph, and Vikas sells it.
Mobs attack the slum in religious riots and the brothers' mother is killed.
The orphaned boys take in a girl, Chandni, sheltering in the rain, and Vikas calls her the third musketeer.
The gangster Dabral collects the street children, feeds them, and trains them to beg.
Aarav sees Dabral blind a boy with acid to make him a better earner, and the three children run for a train.
Vikas lets go of Chandni's hand as the train pulls away, leaving her to Dabral's men.
The brothers live on the trains, stealing food and running tourist scams at a great marble tomb.
Aarav makes Vikas go back to the city to look for Chandni, and they find her being trained as a dancer for Dabral.
Vikas shoots Dabral dead, delivers himself and Chandni to the gangster Rehan, and then throws Aarav out at gunpoint and keeps her.
Aarav takes a job serving tea in a call centre and uses the customer database to find Vikas's number.
Aarav finds Vikas working as Rehan's driver, and finds Chandni living in Rehan's house as his woman.
Aarav arranges to meet Chandni at the station, but Rehan's men catch her, slash her face and move her out of the city.
Knowing Chandni watches it, Aarav gets onto a television quiz show and answers question after question correctly.
The disbelieving host feeds Aarav a wrong answer in the bathroom mirror, and Aarav ignores it.
Aarav is arrested and tortured by police who cannot believe a slum boy could know the answers.
Aarav explains that every answer came out of his own life, and the inspector decides he is telling the truth and releases him for the final question.
Vikas gives Chandni his phone and his car keys and lets her go, then sits in a bathtub full of Rehan's money and kills Rehan and himself.
Chandni answers Aarav's phone-a-friend call without knowing the answer, and Aarav guesses correctly and wins the top prize.
Aarav and Chandni find each other on the platform at the central station.
S24: Police and security services seal off the old square of a European city for a counter-terrorism summit.
In a television truck at the edge of the square, producer Dana Kroll directs the live coverage and argues with her crew over the shots.
Security officer Cale Brody, on duty after taking a bullet for the head of state, works the crowd with his partner Renner.
A local policeman named Marco is drawn away from his post by his girlfriend Pilar, who is part of the plot without his knowing it.
A tourist, Gil Farrow, films the square on his camcorder and catches faces nobody else notices.
A double stands in for the head of state on the podium and is shot twice by a sniper.
Two devices detonate, one among the crowd and one beneath the platform, killing dozens.
Brody sees Marco running from the square and chases him through the streets, convinced he is a bomber.
Renner, secretly part of the plot, is exposed and shot dead by his own conspirators.
The mastermind Valero and his team take the real head of state out of a hotel safe room and drive him away in an ambulance.
Brody gets hold of Farrow's camcorder and identifies the conspirators on the footage.
Pilar learns that her brother Tomas has been forced into the plot by a hostage held over him, and she is killed.
Brody commandeers a car and chases the ambulance across the city.
Tomas is ordered to detonate his vest and refuses once he sees that his own brother is safe.
The ambulance swerves to avoid Farrow, who has run into the road after a lost child, and crashes.
Valero is shot dead, the head of state is pulled out of the wreck alive, and Brody collapses from his injuries.
S22: In Hollow Creek, Errol Doone looks into the eye of the witch in the swamp and sees how he will die, and so knows he will survive everything before it.
Errol grows into the town's champion at everything and saves Hollow Creek from the giant Torvald by befriending him.
Errol and Torvald leave together and part at a fork in the road, Errol taking the hard path through the woods.
Errol stumbles into a hidden town called Willow, where nobody wears shoes and nobody ever leaves, and meets a little girl called Pella.
Errol leaves Willow anyway and joins the ringmaster Grubb's circus, working unpaid for one fact a month about a girl he glimpsed across the tent.
Errol learns the girl is Marguerite, fills a field with daffodils for her, and takes a beating from her fiance Byrne.
Errol marries Marguerite and is drafted into the war, where he steals secret papers and is carried home by a pair of conjoined singers.
Reported dead, Errol walks back into Marguerite's life, and Byrne drops dead of a heart attack.
Errol becomes a travelling salesman away from home for stretches at a time and robs a bank with the poet Lomax.
Errol tells his tall tales at his son Sam's birth and at every family occasion.
Errol hijacks Sam's wedding reception with the story of catching the uncatchable catfish using his own wedding ring as bait.
Humiliated, Sam stops speaking to his father.
Errol goes back to Willow, finds it derelict and repossessed, buys the town to save it, and meets the grown Pella.
Sam, living abroad with his pregnant wife Ilse, is told by his mother that Errol is dying.
Sam comes home and tries to get one true story out of his father, who will only tell the same tales.
Sam finds the deed to Willow among the papers and drives out to meet Pella, who tells him the truth: Errol never left Marguerite.
Errol has a stroke, and from his hospital bed he asks Sam to tell him how he dies.
Sam invents an ending in which he carries his father to the river and Errol turns into a great silver fish and swims away, and Errol dies happy.
At the funeral every character from the stories turns up, ordinary and real, and Sam sees how much of it was true after all.
Sam tells the same stories to his own small son by the river.
S26: An opening sequence relates three improbable coincidences, the last of them a boy who leaps from a rooftop and is shot on the way down by his own mother.
Television producer Ward Halbrook walked out on his dying wife and their son, who reinvented himself as the seduction guru Dean Royce.
Hal Slade, host of a children's quiz show, abused his daughter Nadine, who has not spoken to him.
Bertie Sloan was a famous quiz-show child star whose parents kept every cent of his winnings.
Ward Halbrook, dying of cancer, is nursed at home by a male nurse called Pell while his young wife Rhoda comes apart.
Hal Slade learns he has months to live and tells his wife Beth that he cannot go on.
The quiz kid Milo is driven to another taping by a father living off him.
Nadine takes cocaine alone with the stereo at full volume, and a neighbour calls the police.
Officer Tam answers the call, is charmed by Nadine and asks her out, then loses his gun on a call and spends the day hunting for it.
Dean Royce works a hall of men through his seminar Conquer and Discard and is ambushed in an interview about the father he claims is dead.
Rhoda goes from lawyer to pharmacy in a rage, trying to have Ward's will changed so that she gets nothing.
Pell tracks Dean down by telephone and begs him to come and see his dying father.
Bertie, in love with a bartender, decides to steal from the office that has sacked him.
Milo wets himself on air and refuses to answer another question, and the show collapses live.
Hal breaks down on camera and admits to Beth that he did what Nadine says he did.
Rhoda swallows her pills in the car and is found by a neighbourhood boy who takes her money before calling for help.
Dean arrives at his father's bedside and screams at the unconscious man, then weeps over him.
Hal raises a gun to his own head just as frogs begin falling out of the sky over the valley.
The rain of frogs wrecks cars across the valley and knocks Bertie off the pole he is climbing, and Tam picks him up and lets him put the money back.
Ward dies, Rhoda is taken to hospital, Milo tells his father to be nicer to him, and Nadine turns to Tam and smiles.
S29: Saxophonist Alden Frey suspects his wife Lorna of an affair and cannot reach her in bed or anywhere else.
Unmarked tapes begin turning up at the door, showing first the outside of the house, then its rooms, then the two of them asleep.
At a party Alden meets a pale stranger who tells him he is inside Alden's house at that moment and hands him a phone that proves it.
A tape arrives showing Alden standing over Lorna's dismembered body.
Alden is convicted of her murder and put on death row.
Blinding headaches take hold in the cell, and Alden is gone and a young mechanic named Cully Boone is in his place.
Baffled police release Cully to his parents, who will not say what they saw when he appeared.
Cully goes back to work at the garage, where the gangster Mr. Vance is a favoured customer.
Mr. Vance brings his girlfriend Sunny Keele, Lorna's double as a blonde, to the garage, and she and Cully begin an affair.
Sunny tells Cully that Mr. Vance - the pornographer Rolf Dane - forced her into his films at gunpoint.
Mr. Vance telephones Cully and puts the pale stranger on to explain what happens to men who sleep with his girlfriend.
Sunny talks Cully into robbing and killing the fence Perry so the two of them can run.
Cully kills Perry by accident and sees a photograph of Sunny and Lorna together in Mr. Vance's world.
Sunny and Cully drive to a cabin in the desert and have sex on the sand, and she tells him he will never have her.
Sunny walks into the cabin and the man who stands up outside is Alden Frey.
The pale stranger films Alden at the cabin and tells him that the woman's name is Lorna.
Alden takes Mr. Vance into the desert, cuts his throat with the stranger's help, and is shown a screen playing his life back at him.
Alden drives to his own house and speaks into the intercom the words the film opened with: "Rolf Dane is dead."
The police give chase down the road as Alden's face distorts and the film ends where it began.
S27: Helicopters spray the city for crop pests, passing over every neighbourhood in the film.
Doctor Neil Hartigan and his wife Bess, a painter, get ready for a dinner party.
The baker Otto Kemp takes an order for a birthday cake for a boy called Charlie Rill.
Charlie is knocked down by a car driven by a waitress called Rhona on his way to school and walks home insisting he is fine.
Charlie collapses into a coma, and his parents Grant and Elaine keep vigil at the hospital.
Grant's estranged father Duff turns up at the hospital and confesses an affair.
Unpaid and ignored, the baker starts making anonymous menacing phone calls to the family.
Telephone-sex worker Cheryl talks men through their fantasies from her living room while her husband Stu seethes beside her.
Stu and three friends drive out to fish and find a young woman's body face down in the river.
The men tether the body to the bank and carry on fishing before telling anyone.
Vern's wife Iris, a party clown, is disgusted when she learns what the men did.
The singer Vida performs in a club while her cellist daughter Bee plays alone at home.
Officer Rowe, cheating on his wife Peg with a woman called Nan, abandons the family dog to cover one of his lies.
Nan's ex-husband Cass, a helicopter pilot, learns she has a new man and saws her furniture to pieces.
Ike and Dot house-sit for the Hartigans and photograph Dot made up as a beaten corpse.
At the dinner party Bess admits to a nude modelling session and an affair, and Neil makes a scene.
Charlie dies in hospital, and Grant and Elaine go to the bakery to confront Otto, who feeds them warm bread and grieves with them.
Bee finds her mother asleep, closes the garage door and kills herself with the car engine running.
At a picnic in the hills Stu smashes a young woman's head with a rock.
A tremor shakes the entire city, and every death and every wreck is folded into one evening bulletin.
S28: Dana Reeve wins a dance contest in a small northern town and comes to the film capital on her dead aunt's money.
Dana meets the actress Vivien Loy on the set of a picture called The Undertow, loses the lead to her, and becomes her lover.
Vivien gets Dana bit parts out of pity while her own career takes off.
Vivien ends the affair, and Dana keeps calling her.
Vivien drives Dana up the canyon road to a party at the director Gil Barron's house.
At the party Vivien kisses another actress and she and Gil announce their engagement while Dana sits humiliated at the table.
In a coffee shop Dana pays a hitman to kill Vivien, and he tells her she will find a blue key when it is done.
Dana wakes on her sofa, finds the blue key on the table, and begins to come apart.
In her dream Dana recasts herself as the fresh-faced Elise, arriving in the film capital to stay in her aunt's flat.
A woman survives a staged crash on the canyon road, walks down into the city with no memory, and hides in that same flat, calling herself Zora after a poster.
Elise and Zora find a handbag stuffed with cash and a blue key, and set out to discover who Zora is.
A contract killer's straightforward job collapses into farce and leaves three corpses.
Gil Barron is forced by the mob and by a man in a wide hat to cast an unknown blonde named Vivien Loy in his film.
A man in the coffee shop describes a nightmare about a figure behind the building and drops dead of fright when he sees it.
Elise auditions brilliantly and is taken to Gil's set, where their eyes meet across the sound stage.
Elise and Zora find a rotting corpse in Dana Reeve's flat and flee.
Elise and Zora become lovers, and Zora takes them to a theatre called the Vellum where everything turns out to be a recording.
Elise finds a blue box in her handbag, Zora opens it with the blue key, and both women vanish out of the dream.
Awake and ruined, Dana hallucinates her miniature parents shrieking at her heels and shoots herself on her bed.
The man in the wide hat looks in at the door, the old couple crawl under it, and a woman in the balcony of the Vellum says "silence".
S32: Four engineers - Kell, Orrin, Dov and Prentice - build error-checking devices in a garage, funded by whatever they can sell.
Kell and Orrin cut the other two out and build a box that unexpectedly reduces the weight of anything placed inside it.
A protein accumulates inside a test object at a rate implying it sat in the field longer than the machine was switched on.
Orrin works out that the box loops matter back through time and builds a man-sized version in a rented storage unit.
Orrin uses it alone, doubling back six hours to prove it works, and tells Kell what he has done.
Orrin walks Kell through the protocol: switch the box on, stay sealed in a hotel room, ride it back, and never meet your other self.
The pair begin making day-long returns to trade shares whose closing prices they already know.
Kell admits he has built a third box, has been going back further than agreed, and has been carrying a recorder.
Kell lives through a party at the Ledgers' house over and over, rehearsing until he can talk down Nora's ex-boyfriend, who arrives with a shotgun.
Nora's father Owen turns up as a double who has come back from days ahead, and is found half-conscious in a car.
Owen's double collapses when Kell and Orrin confront him and lapses into a coma.
Orrin reveals a failsafe box, switched on before he told Kell about any of it, that can take him back to before it all started.
Orrin uses the failsafe to return to the beginning and stop his earlier self from entering the machine.
Kell, who found and used the failsafe first, is waiting; he drugs the earlier Orrin and takes his place.
Kell narrates the whole account down the phone to a version of Orrin on a plane bound overseas.
Orrin stays behind to dismantle the machines and keep his other self away from them.
Kell builds a full-sized box in a warehouse overseas, using workers who cannot read the plans.
S33: Elliot Farb grows up in a house under a seaside amusement pier, depressed because the universe is expanding.
At school Elliot kisses a girl in class, and his classmates stand up one by one to announce what they grew up to be.
Elliot does his army service entertaining troops and becomes a stand-up comedian in the city.
Elliot's first marriage, to Judith, fails while he obsesses over a political assassination in bed.
Elliot's second marriage, to Carol, fails amid literary parties and her refusal to be interrupted.
Elliot meets Peggy Rowan after a tennis game with his friend Max, and she drives him home terrifyingly and asks him up for wine.
Elliot and Peggy's first date ends in bed, and she needs a cigarette.
Peggy moves in with Elliot, who pushes her into adult-education classes and books about death.
Elliot sends Peggy to an analyst and pays for it, and their two sessions are played side by side in split screen.
Elliot and Peggy visit her family in a farm town, where her grandmother stares at him and he sees himself at the table as a figure from another century.
Peggy's brother Neil confides his urge to steer into oncoming headlights, and drives them to the airport.
Elliot and Peggy break up, and each of them tries seeing other people.
Peggy calls Elliot about a spider in the bathroom, and they get back together.
Peggy starts singing in clubs and is courted professionally by the record producer Sy Kale.
Elliot and Peggy fly to the coast for a television award, and Elliot hates every minute of it.
On the flight back each of them concedes, in unspoken narration, that it has ended.
Elliot flies back to the coast to propose, is turned down in a health-food restaurant, and crashes a rental car.
Elliot writes a play in which the woman says yes, and admits to the audience that you can do that in art.
Elliot and Peggy meet in the city as friends, and he watches her walk away.
Elliot tells the joke about the man whose brother thinks he is a chicken, and says relationships are irrational but we keep going through them anyway.
S37: The assassin code-named Mantis leaves the Adder Unit for the child she is carrying and plans a wedding in a desert chapel under a new name.
Corvin and the rest of the unit walk into the wedding rehearsal and massacre everyone in the chapel.
Corvin shoots Mantis through the head, and she survives in a coma.
Reiko Sana, whose parents were murdered in front of her, kills the boss responsible and grows up to be a top assassin.
Reiko takes the eastern capital's underworld by beheading a rival at a council meeting, and rules it with the schoolgirl killer Momo and the lawyer Delphine.
The one-eyed Dara comes to the hospital to kill the comatose Mantis with a syringe and is called off by Corvin.
An orderly called Wade sells the comatose woman's body to visitors.
Mantis wakes, kills Wade and his customer, and finds her belly flat and her baby gone.
She lies in the back of Wade's truck until she can move her toes.
Mantis writes out her list of five names and drives to Odette Bray's house in the suburbs.
The two fight through the kitchen, break off when Odette's small daughter comes home from school, and Mantis kills Odette with a thrown knife in front of the child.
Mantis flies to a southern island and talks the retired swordsmith Ito into making her a blade to kill his own former student, Corvin.
In the eastern capital Mantis cuts Delphine's arm off outside a restaurant called the Lantern and sends her to Corvin as a message.
Mantis kills Momo and then fights her way through the Eighty across the restaurant.
Mantis duels Reiko in the snow garden and takes off the top of her skull.
She interrogates the maimed Delphine in the boot of a car and leaves her alive to tell Corvin everything.
Corvin asks Delphine whether Mantis knows that her daughter is alive.
S39: Leaflets fall on the port and enemy fire drives the private Ives through the streets to the beach, the only one of his patrol to make it.
Ives meets a silent soldier called Marne burying a body, and the two carry a wounded man onto a hospital ship to get themselves aboard.
They are put off the ship again, and it is bombed and goes down in the harbour behind them.
Ives, Marne and a corporal called Beckett hide in a beached trawler outside the perimeter, waiting for the tide to lift it.
Enemy soldiers use the trawler for target practice, and the men inside argue about throwing Marne overboard to lighten it.
The trawler floods and Marne drowns, and the survivors swim clear into a burning oil slick.
The harbour commander Dyer watches from the mole as ship after ship is sunk and the perimeter shrinks around the beach.
In the home port the civilian sailor Whitlock takes his boat Kestrel out himself with his son Nate and their friend Row rather than surrender her to the navy.
They pick a shivering soldier off the hull of a wrecked ship, and he panics when he learns where they are heading.
In the struggle Row is thrown down the ladder and blinded, and he dies in the cabin.
Three fighters cross the water; the leader is shot down and the pilot Ryland takes over with a smashed fuel gauge.
His wingman Poole is hit and ditches in the sea, and his canopy jams as the aircraft fills and sinks.
Whitlock brings Kestrel alongside and Nate smashes the canopy in to pull Poole out.
Ryland shoots down the bomber attacking the minesweeper, saving the men in the water and on the mole.
Kestrel reaches the oil slick and takes Ives, Beckett and others aboard as the fuel catches fire.
Ryland, out of fuel, glides the length of the beach, brings down one more aircraft, lands past the perimeter and burns his fighter before he is taken prisoner.
The little ships arrive and the evacuation succeeds, and Dyer stays behind for the allied troops waiting.
Ives and Beckett reach home expecting contempt and are handed beer and blankets, and Ives reads the prime minister's speech aloud from a newspaper.
S40: Scavenging in the closed city of Vyrsk, Yuri Sarkin finds a buried cache of gold and a message from the future, and is hired to assemble the Device.
The scientist who built the Device splits it into nine pieces, hides them in the past, and kills herself so that it cannot be rebuilt.
Dying of cancer, Sarkin decides to take the world with him by assembling the Device and reversing entropy.
An intelligence operative survives a siege at a concert hall and swallows a cyanide pill that turns out to be a loyalty test, and is recruited into the organisation.
The operative is shown inverted bullets and briefed by a scientist on objects whose entropy runs backwards.
He traces the bullets to the arms dealer Devi, who names Sarkin as the source.
An official called Ballard tells him to reach Sarkin through his estranged wife Ana, an art appraiser trapped by a forged painting she authenticated.
The operative and Vidal break into the airport freeport to steal the forgery and are attacked by a masked man moving backwards through the fight.
Ana introduces the operative to Sarkin, who tries to have him killed on the yacht.
Sarkin takes the operative along on a raid to seize a radioactive core from a motorway convoy in the coastal city.
The operative hides the case, Sarkin shoots Ana with an inverted bullet, and the operative gives up the case to save her.
The operative and Vidal invert themselves and drive the convoy chase backwards to recover the case, and the operative fights the masked man in the freeport - himself.
The inverted Ana is taken back through the freeport turnstile to be healed before the radiation kills her.
The team work out that Sarkin's dead-man switch will detonate the Device at the moment of his death, on a yacht off a southern coast.
A temporal pincer movement is mounted at Vyrsk, with one team moving forward and one backward through the same ten minutes.
On the yacht, Ana keeps Sarkin alive until the signal comes, and then kills him herself.
In the hypocentre, the operative and a soldier reach the Device, and a corpse with a red-tagged rucksack opens the gate for them.
Vidal reveals that he was that corpse, that he has known the operative from the other direction, and goes back to die.
The operative kills Devi to protect Ana and her son, and understands that he is himself the founder of the organisation who recruited them all.
S43: Nell Prior is sacked from her public-relations job and heads home.
She runs down the steps to the underground, and the story splits at the closing doors of the train.
In the first branch she catches the train, meets Owen, and gets home to find her boyfriend Craig in bed with his ex, Tamsin.
She leaves Craig and moves in with her friend Cleo.
She cuts and dyes her hair and starts an agency of her own with Owen egging her on.
In the second branch she misses the train, is mugged on the way out, and reaches the flat after Tamsin has gone.
She takes two jobs, delivering sandwiches and pulling pints, to keep Craig writing his unwritten novel.
Craig keeps seeing Tamsin and keeps lying about it, and Tamsin starts pressing him to choose.
In the first branch Nell and Owen fall in love, and Nell learns she is pregnant.
Nell sees Owen with another woman, assumes he is married, and walks out on him.
In the second branch Nell finds she is pregnant by Craig and plans to tell him over dinner.
Tamsin turns up at the same restaurant and tells Craig that she is pregnant too.
In the first branch Owen finds Nell and explains that the woman is his wife, whom he is divorcing.
Nell steps into the road and is hit by a car, and both branches converge on the same hospital.
In the first branch Nell loses the baby and dies with Owen beside her.
In the second branch Nell loses the baby but survives, and throws Craig out.
Leaving the hospital in a lift, Nell drops an earring and a stranger picks it up: Owen.
S42: At a religious school, Bruno Malvasi sneaks down to the beach to watch the prostitute Mareva dance, and is beaten for it by the priests.
Bruno's mother watches over him from the edge of every memory, and he loses her.
Bruno becomes the country's most celebrated director, with a run of hits and a public that hangs on his every word.
Bruno marries the actress Renata, who gives up her own career for him.
Bruno takes a mistress, Gilda, and installs her in hotels near wherever he happens to be shooting.
Bruno's last two films fail, and he finds he cannot write the next one.
A press conference in the capital for the unwritten film Aurora turns into an ambush, and Bruno flees to a spa on the coast.
His costume designer and confidante Zita tells him plainly that he has nothing to say.
Gilda follows him to the spa, checks into his hotel and stages an elaborate seduction.
Bruno summons his muse, the star Adriana, and cannot tell her what the part is.
The producer begins erecting sets for a picture with no screenplay, while the crew idles on the lot.
Renata arrives at the spa and sees Gilda's name in the hotel register.
Told to leave, Gilda takes an overdose in her room and survives it.
Bruno imagines every woman in his life singing for him at once on an empty soundstage.
Renata confronts Bruno in front of the press and tells him she is done being his material.
Bruno abandons the film on the day shooting was to start, and the sets are struck.
Bruno spends time in silence, until Zita talks him into trying.
Bruno calls Renata to a screen test for a film about the two of them, and she agrees to sit and watch.
S45: Solly Two Coats and his crew rob a diamond house in a northern port dressed as devout pilgrims and walk out with a huge stone.
His cousin Marv, overseas, tells Solly to bring the stone straight over.
Grigor the Nail tells Solly about a bookmaker's in the city and tips off the pawnbrokers Ike and Benno to rob him there.
Boxing promoters Halloway and Digby send the fighter Pretty Sam to buy a caravan from a camp of travellers.
The bare-knuckle fighter Finn knocks Sam out over the deal, leaving Halloway without a man for the gang boss Coldstone's fixed bout.
Halloway has to put Finn in the fight instead, and promises Coldstone that Finn will go down in the fourth round.
Solly lands in the city, delivers the stone to the fence Hersch, and heads for the bookmaker's to bet on the fight.
Ike, Benno and Tulley bungle the robbery, take Solly's arm and his case, and are chased off by Grigor.
Finn knocks his opponent out cold in the first round, and Coldstone loses a fortune and takes it out on Halloway.
Marv flies in, finds Solly gone, and hires the bounty hunter Ledge to find him.
Grigor takes Solly, cuts off his arm to get the case open, and finds that the stone is not inside it.
Ledge traces the pawnbrokers, shoots their car to pieces and takes both them and the stone.
Coldstone feeds Solly to his pigs and tells Halloway and Digby what will happen to them if the second fight goes wrong.
Halloway and Digby tell Finn to go down in the fourth, and Coldstone's men burn Finn's mother to death in her caravan.
Grigor ambushes Ledge's car with Ike and Benno inside, and in the shootout Ledge, Grigor and Benno are all killed.
Tulley gets away with the dog that has swallowed the diamond.
Finn knocks his opponent out in the fourth round, and the travellers massacre Coldstone's men in the crowd.
Halloway and Digby find Coldstone and shoot him, and the travellers have vanished.
The dog is handed in at a pet shop, coughs up the diamond, and Halloway and Digby end up holding it.
S47: Over a black screen, emergency calls from inside burning towers are heard during a coordinated attack on the country's largest city.
A source hands the agency the real name of a courier for the fugitive leader, Nabil Rasheed, and the report is filed away and forgotten.
The analyst Reyna arrives at a secret site overseas and watches her colleague Kessner waterboard a detainee called Faris.
Broken by sleep deprivation and humiliation, Faris gives up the existence of a courier known only as Sahim.
Reyna works the detainee network, chasing the name through interrogations on three continents.
Bombings in a European capital and at a hotel in the region go off around her.
Reyna's colleague Fay cultivates an informant who kills her and six others with a suicide vest at a forward base.
Reyna survives an assassination attempt by gunmen outside her compound.
A detainee's account is matched against the buried report, and Sahim is identified as Nabil Rasheed.
Reyna has the courier's mother's phone tapped, and he is located in a northern city.
Surveillance follows the courier's white four-wheel drive to a fortified compound in a garrison town with no telephone line and no internet.
Reyna insists the compound is the fugitive leader's, and the agency director demands to know how certain she is.
The station chief and the analysts argue the probability down to sixty per cent, and Reyna says one hundred.
The government authorises a helicopter raid rather than an air strike, and two stealth helicopters are prepared.
A special-operations unit flies into the garrison town, and one helicopter's tail clips the compound wall as it lands.
The unit clears the house floor by floor, killing the courier, his brother and one of the leader's sons.
On the top floor they shoot the fugitive leader dead and carry the body out as the crippled helicopter is destroyed.
Reyna identifies the body in a hangar at a forward airfield.
Reyna boards a transport plane alone, is asked where she wants to go, and has no answer.
S46: Border-city police officers Nuno and Tavo intercept a drug shipment in the desert and have it taken off them by the army commander Obrero's men.
Obrero recruits Nuno onto his anti-cartel task force, which is in fact a front for the northern cartel.
Nuno helps capture the coastal cartel's enforcer Paz, who is tortured into naming the hit man Blanco.
Across the border, federal drug agents Brand and Dell arrest the mid-level dealer Nando Cano and turn him into a witness.
Cano's testimony brings the arrest of the importer Rafael Solis in front of his pregnant wife Nadia, who knows nothing about the business.
Judge Warren Bell is appointed the country's drug policy director and briefed in the capital on a war nobody there thinks can be won.
Bell's daughter Simone and her friends free-base at a party, and one of them nearly dies of it.
Nadia discovers that the family is bankrupt and that the cartel is threatening her son over her husband's debts.
Nadia goes to Rafael's lawyer Metz and then arranges a meeting with the coastal cartel's brothers herself.
Simone's habit moves from cocaine to heroin, and she is arrested and thrown out of school.
Nadia commissions Blanco to kill Cano before he can testify.
Bell tours the border, meets Obrero, and is told by everyone he talks to that treatment is the only thing that works.
Simone runs away and starts prostituting herself for drugs in an inner-city motel.
Blanco's car bomb kills Dell instead of Cano.
Bell abandons his official duties and searches the motels of his own state for his daughter himself.
Tavo tries to sell what he knows about Obrero to the agents and is executed in the desert in front of Nuno.
Blanco poisons Cano in protective custody, and the case against Rafael Solis collapses.
Nuno gives Obrero up to the agents, and the commander is exposed as the northern cartel's man and arrested.
Bell resigns at his own press conference, saying he cannot fight a war against his own family.
Brand plants a bug at the party celebrating Rafael's release, Nadia takes over running the business, and Nuno watches the floodlit baseball game he asked for as his price.
S53: On a city rooftop a young composer, his lyricist and their writer friend watch a new satellite cross the sky and swear to each other that they will make something worth making.
The composer and the lyricist turn out songs in a cramped flat while their friend begins a novel.
The composer marries a singer, and the three of them live off sketch material for revues.
Their revue opens in a small theatre, and the wife of the man backing it takes a close interest in the composer.
The composer and the singer have a son.
The composer and the backer's wife begin an affair at a party in her own house, with his wife looking on.
The singer divorces him and is awarded custody of the boy in court.
The composer and the lyricist have a genuine hit, and the composer starts mounting other people's shows instead of writing his own.
On a live broadcast the lyricist performs a public denunciation of his partner, and the collaboration ends on the air.
The novel is dismissed by every critic who reviews it, and its author starts drinking seriously.
The composer marries the backer's wife and moves west to produce pictures.
At a party at his house on the coast, his second wife throws acid into the face of his young mistress.
At the same party his oldest friend, very drunk, tells him he has thrown away everything he ever had, and leaves for good.
S50: Davey Lurie pawns his mother Golda's television for drug money, and Golda buys it back from the same shop.
Davey, his friend Cyrus and his girlfriend Petra plan to buy weight, cut it, and use the profit to open a shop for Petra's designs.
Alone in her seafront flat, Golda is telephoned with news that she has been chosen to appear on a television game show.
Golda cannot fit into the red dress she wore to Davey's graduation, and starts a diet of grapefruit and hard-boiled eggs.
Davey and Cyrus make their first good buy, and the money starts coming in.
A doctor prescribes Golda amphetamines without examining her, and the weight starts falling off.
Petra breaks with her parents' money and starts drawing, and she and Davey imagine the shop together.
Cyrus is caught up in a shooting at a street deal, and the supply dries up across the city.
Golda doubles her pills, starts grinding her teeth, and hallucinates the refrigerator advancing across the kitchen.
Davey's arm becomes infected at the injection site, and the three of them start using more than they can sell.
Petra sleeps with her psychiatrist Dr. Nolan for money to buy drugs.
Cyrus is arrested in a raid, and Davey spends the last of their money bailing him out.
Starving and alone, Golda hallucinates herself onto the game show and is jeered at by the studio audience.
Golda walks to the television company's offices in a stained coat and collapses in reception.
Davey and Cyrus drive south on a rumour of pure heroin, with Davey's arm turning black on the way.
Petra goes to a dealer called Ray and takes part in a sex party for a bag of heroin.
Golda is committed, force-fed and given electroconvulsive therapy while her friends wait outside the ward.
Davey's arm is amputated at a southern hospital, where the police are called about the needle marks.
Cyrus is put on a prison work gang, sick with withdrawal and dreaming of his mother.
Each of the four curls into the same foetal position - Davey in his bed, Petra clutching her bag, Golda staring at a screen, Cyrus in his bunk.
S51: During a party at the house of his closest friend, a book agent named Wilder leads Odile to an upstairs room and tells her how lovely she is while the other guests drink downstairs.
Wilder and Odile rent rooms in a quiet district and fill them with linen and plates, giving the affair a household of its own.
Odile says she is carrying her husband's child, and the pair decide the rented rooms will go on exactly as before.
In a hotel abroad, her husband Emlyn asks about a letter held for her at the desk, addressed in a hand he recognises.
Odile confesses, and Emlyn remarks that he is fonder of his friend than of his wife.
Odile goes back to the rented rooms and says nothing whatever about the trip, and the afternoon passes exactly as the others have.
Emlyn drinks through a long restaurant lunch with Wilder, baiting him about contemporary fiction and never once mentioning what he has learned.
Over dinner at the married couple's house the two men discuss racquet games and schoolboy sport until Odile has no part in the talk at all.
Wilder and Odile decide the rented rooms have become a chore, split the crockery and surrender the lease.
In a bar, Odile tells Wilder her marriage is over and that she spent a night confessing everything to her husband.
Odile lets slip that Emlyn has been publishing a writer whom Wilder represents and whom the two men both quietly detest.
Wilder rings Emlyn in a state and Emlyn comes to his house.
Emlyn says he has known, that his wife told him on the trip abroad, and that he never thought much of his friend's letters either.
S52: Dreading conscription, a young man and his closest friend agree to end their lives together; the friend dies and the young man is discovered still breathing.
The survivor is convicted over the death and taken away to serve a sentence.
A typist starts an affair with a soldier who has a wife at home, meeting him on packed trains and in unlit streets.
Steering an ambulance through bombing, a woman in trousers pulls another woman out of a house that has come down.
The pair share a flat, one of them jealous of everyone the other knew first and lying about small things.
The younger of the two meets an old lover of her partner's, and the two of them start an affair kept carefully hidden.
The typist bleeds badly after a backstreet termination in a hired room, and the soldier walks out and leaves her there.
The ambulance driver finds her bleeding, gets her to a hospital, and slides her own gold band onto the girl's finger so the nurses will assume a husband.
The convicted man shares a cell with an objector who keeps pressing him about what he is really being punished for.
The ambulance driver lodges alone in a rented room, walking the streets in men's clothes with nothing left to occupy her.
The two lovers live together while one of them goes through the other's pockets and letters hunting for a betrayal she cannot name.
The typist takes a desk at a marriage agency and meets her soldier in hotel rooms, the borrowed gold band shut in a drawer.
The released man keeps house for an elderly lodger until the objector from his cell arrives at the door and unsettles the whole arrangement.
S54: At a works outing beside a stream, a young man sits away from the crowd with a girl from the packing line and tells her he intends to take photographs for a living.
The girl presses a tin of mints into his hand, and he watches a goods train pass with the feeling that everything is about to begin.
Called up, he is sent with his company to break a rising in a provincial city and takes a bullet through the calf.
Bleeding and terrified in the dark, he fires at a shape in a doorway and kills a schoolgirl who was trying to get home.
As a detective, he beats a student in a cell and finds that the work suits him.
The girl from the packing line brings him a camera she has saved up for; he refuses it and spends the night with a waitress.
He tortures an organiser in a country town, then washes his hands and sits down to a bowl of rice.
He marries a good-humoured woman he does not love and lets his colleagues arrange the whole wedding.
He runs a small furniture firm, strikes his wife, and learns she is sleeping with the man teaching her to drive.
He follows her, catches the two of them and beats the man, then returns to a mistress of his own.
The firm fails, his partner takes what money is left, and his wife walks out.
He buys a pistol and drives about the city unable to settle on who deserves it.
The husband of the girl from the packing line brings him to her hospital bed, where she is dying and cannot speak, and returns the camera she once bought.
He forces his way into a reunion picnic beside the same stream, climbs onto a railway bridge, and stands facing an oncoming train shouting that he wants to go back.
S56: A boy is born in the family mansion and carried up to a nursery draped in white gauze.
He crawls under the furniture and comes to know the house by its undersides and its smells.
He is dressed in his first stiff clothes and taught to sit through long formal dinners without moving.
He gambles, drinks and keeps company with singers in the capital.
His father dies and he comes into the title, the mansion and the debts at once.
He marries a young noblewoman in the cathedral.
His wife dies of a fever, and the house fills with candles, black cloth and murmuring relations.
He sells the furniture piece by piece while the creditors start appearing at the door.
He dies in the bed he was born in as a priest gives him the last rites.
The mourners disperse and the shutters of the mansion are fastened.
Labourers take the mansion down course by course while a man leaning on a stick watches from the gate.
Nothing remains on the site but bare earth, and the palms and the grass stand where the walls used to be.
S55: On a southern beach a woman notices a man who is holidaying at the same hotel with his girlfriend.
The girlfriend flies home after a row, and the man knocks at the woman's door.
The two of them wade out into the sea together as the sun goes down.
At their wedding in a country hotel her estranged parents are seated at opposite ends of the table and every speech is cold.
He passes out drunk, and she lets a stranger in from the corridor.
Their son is delivered by emergency surgery while the father sits in the car park unable to make himself go inside.
He arrives on the ward and admits where he has been.
Over dinner for his brother and his brother's boyfriend, he describes watching strangers have sex at a club.
She says at the same table that she was there and watched too, and the evening turns.
The couple begin sleeping in separate rooms, and he takes a lover at his office.
A clerk in a lawyer's office reads out the terms of the divorce and the two of them sign it.
They take a hotel room, sleep together, and he dresses and leaves her lying on the bed.
S57: A young man grows up in a small provincial town on the continent and qualifies in medicine.
He marries, and the child born to the couple dies as an infant.
He takes a post at an institute where the disabled are put to death by injection and by gas.
He is posted to a camp in the east and stands beside the senior physician during selections on the platform.
Inside the camp he performs dental procedures and experiments on the prisoners.
He takes a prisoner as a mistress and sends her to the chamber once he has tired of her.
The camp is cleared before the advancing army arrives and he walks west with forged papers in his coat.
He spends time in hiding on the southern coast under an assumed name, living quietly on gold.
He crosses the ocean under a second false name, given fresh papers by a clergyman who asks him nothing.
Working in hospitals abroad, he inflicts pain on his patients and persuades himself that he is curing them.
He carries on a long affair with a woman who never learns a single true thing about him.
He lives under a third name, gardening, hoarding tinned food, and waking from dreams of a man in a white coat.
He collapses among his flowerbeds and dies in a hospital far from where he began.
S59: Two inseparable schoolgirls sit the entrance examination for a selective school and both of them pass.
One girl's stepfather refuses to let her take the place, saying the uniform and the fees are out of reach.
The other girl starts at the selective school in the new uniform on her own.
The first girl stays at the local school and begins going round with older boys.
Her mother and stepfather fight through the evenings and she starts staying out at night.
The second girl's mother makes it clear she considers her daughter's friend a bad influence.
The first girl leaves home and moves into a shared house with a boy she barely knows.
She dyes her hair, takes work behind a counter and stops going to school at all.
The second girl visits the shared house and is frightened by what she sees.
The two of them quarrel at a party and stop speaking.
The second girl settles at her new school, makes new friends and wins a prize for music.
The first girl appears at her old friend's front door and neither of them can think of anything to say.
S58: A butcher marries a local woman and the pair set up home above his shop.
His wife takes a lover, and the butcher works out what has been happening.
The butcher kills his wife and cuts her up on the block in his own shop.
He distributes the pieces about the city in brown paper parcels and a travelling case.
He takes up with a young woman who knows nothing whatever about any of it.
He kills his wife's lover and disposes of him by the same method.
The parcels come to light and the police open a murder inquiry.
The butcher is arrested in his rooms and led away in front of his neighbours.
He stands trial while the court is told what the parcels contained.
He is beheaded in the prison yard.
His body is buried and his belongings are returned to nobody in particular.
S60: A novelist meets a woman from entirely outside the world he was raised in and is elated by her.
Their evening together ends with her telling him about the man she almost settled for.
His first book is taken by a publisher and he is celebrating before he has finished telling her.
She sits through a casting call at which nobody behind the table lifts their eyes from the papers.
He gives her a gift and swears to her that he will never walk out.
She takes a summer engagement at a provincial theatre and writes home from a bare rented room.
His book succeeds and he is made much of at parties she will not go to.
She tells him he has never once come to watch her perform in anything.
A young woman propositions him at a publishing party and he argues himself into it.
