She admits to herself that she cannot make herself glad about her husband's success.
He sleeps with someone else and concedes privately that the marriage is over.
He writes a letter, puts his key on the table and lets himself out.
She comes home to the empty flat and finds the letter.
S63: A divorced woman comes back to her family's house in a river town with her boy and girl twins.
Her aunt makes it plain that she resents the twins and their mother equally.
A carpenter from the lowest caste works at the family's pickle works and is the twins' closest friend.
On the drive to meet a cousin from overseas, a man behind a cinema refreshment counter forces the boy to masturbate him.
The cousin arrives with her mother and the whole household makes a fuss of her.
The divorced woman and the carpenter begin meeting in the dark on the far bank of the river.
The carpenter's father tells the family about the affair.
The woman is locked in her room and shouts through the door that her children are millstones round her neck.
The twins and their cousin row across the river in the dark, the boat turns over, and the cousin drowns.
The aunt tells the police that the carpenter took the children and raped their mother.
The police beat the carpenter almost to death in the ruined house across the river while the twins watch from a doorway.
The aunt makes the boy say the carpenter took them, and the carpenter dies in a cell.
The boy is sent away to his father, and his mother dies alone in a lodging house at thirty-one.
The grown daughter, divorced, returns to the river town and finds the house rotting and her great-aunt watching satellite television all day.
She finds her brother, sent back, walking in the rain and no longer speaking at all.
She goes to the ruined house across the river, a heritage hotel where the old stories are performed for guests.
The twins stand together in the closed pickle works where the vats used to be.
Alone in the house, the twins sleep together.
S61: In the schoolroom of a great country house, a girl of thirteen asks her tutor what a carnal embrace is, having overheard talk about him and a guest's wife in the summerhouse.
A minor poet challenges the tutor to a duel over his wife, and the tutor talks him out of it by promising to praise his verses.
The lady of the house quarrels with her landscape designer over his scheme to replace the park with an artificial wilderness and a hermit's cell.
The tutor writes a savage notice of the poet's book while a celebrated aristocrat staying in the house borrows volumes from the library and quits the country.
The poet and a naval officer sail for the tropics with the poet's wife, and the poet dies out there of a monkey bite.
The girl works out a method of drawing natural shapes by repeated calculation, and grasps that heat only ever travels one way.
She asks her tutor to teach her to waltz, and kisses him.
She dies when her bedroom catches fire.
The tutor becomes the hermit of the estate and fills the cell with calculations until he dies in it.
A writer works in the same room on a book about that hermit and the collapse of Romantic thought.
An academic arrives hunting a scandal and concludes that the celebrated aristocrat shot the poet in a duel and fled abroad because of it.
A biologist in the family is fitting a repeated-calculation model to two centuries of game records kept in the house.
The academic announces his theory in a public lecture and is taken up by the newspapers.
The biologist recognises that the mathematics in the dead girl's exercise book is a version of what he is doing himself.
The writer proves the poet died abroad of a monkey bite, and the academic's theory collapses in public.
The writer identifies the hermit from a figure sketched into the designer's book of plans.
In the final scene the two centuries occupy the room at once, and both couples waltz among each other's papers.
S65: In a working-class quarter, a teenager parks cars for the crew across the road and decides that being a gangster beats being head of state.
He is arrested for selling stolen cigarettes and comes out of court to find the whole crew waiting to congratulate him for saying nothing.
He and two older men hijack lorries out of the airport and move the loads on.
He meets the woman he will marry, and when a neighbour assaults her he pistol-whips the man on his own drive and hands her the gun to hide.
The two marry, and she learns to live with the money, the absences and the other men's wives.
The volatile one of the pair stabs and shoots a protected man in their own club, and the three of them drive the body upstate to bury it.
They have to dig the body up again because the land has been sold.
He installs a mistress in a flat, and his wife finds out and holds a revolver to his face while he sleeps.
He and the older man burn down a restaurant they have stripped through a paper credit line.
He is jailed for beating a gambler who complained to his sister, and runs food and drugs from inside the prison.
He is released and starts dealing heroin against the boss's express orders, pulling in his wife and both friends.
The crew take six million out of the airport cargo terminal in a single night.
The older man has nearly everyone involved killed as they begin spending the money where it can be seen.
The volatile one is told he is to be made and is shot through the head instead, in payment for the protected man.
In one frantic day he runs drugs, cooks a family dinner and is tailed by a helicopter, and is arrested.
The boss gives him a few thousand and disowns him, and the older man tries to send him and his wife to a killing in the south.
He testifies against both of them and enters witness protection, ending up an ordinary man fetching his newspaper in a suburb.
S66: The lead barrister on a class action defending a chemicals conglomerate stops taking his medication.
He strips during a deposition in a midwestern city and runs into the car park announcing that he is the servant of a corrupt design.
The firm's fixer, a ruined gambler, is sent out to bring him back.
The fixer, in debt to loan sharks over a failed restaurant, asks his partners for an advance against his bonus and is turned down.
The conglomerate's general counsel is briefed about the barrister and rehearses her answers alone in a hotel bathroom.
The barrister has obtained an internal memorandum showing the company knew its weedkiller was killing people.
He telephones one of the claimants and orders six hundred bound copies of the memorandum printed.
The general counsel authorises two contractors to put him under full surveillance.
The contractors kill him in his flat and dress it as a suicide by injection.
The fixer refuses to accept the suicide and finds the printer's receipt among the dead man's papers.
His brother's debts and his son's telephone calls close in on him from every direction at once.
He collects the annotated copy of the memorandum from the printers.
The contractors put a device in his car while he has stopped at the roadside to look at three horses in a field.
The car explodes, and he throws his watch and rings into the fire so the body will be taken for his own.
He confronts the general counsel at a board meeting, records her offering him money to keep quiet, and has the police waiting downstairs.
He gets into a taxi, hands the driver fifty dollars and tells him to just drive.
S68: A virus let loose kills most of the human race and drives the survivors below ground.
The scientists running the underground colony send convicts up to gather specimens, and one of them volunteers.
He is sent back through time, arrives too early, and is arrested raving about a plague.
In the asylum a psychiatrist interviews him, and he meets the son of a celebrated virologist.
He is hauled back to the future and questioned about a recorded message the scientists have recovered.
He is sent to the right year and abducts the psychiatrist, who has written a book about apocalyptic prophecy.
The two of them find graffiti for a shadowy group and trace the virologist's son to his father's estate.
The son denies everything and says the idea of stealing the virus was the convict's own, from the asylum.
The psychiatrist comes across a photograph from the great war of a soldier who is unmistakably him.
He decides he has been mad and asks to be allowed to stay where he is.
She finds a bullet fired in the great war in an X-ray of him and realises he has been telling the truth.
The shadowy group turn out to be animal rights activists who free the zoo animals and shut the virologist in a cupboard.
The pair go to the airport in disguise to stop the virologist's assistant, who is the real carrier.
She spots the carrier, he runs at the man with a gun, and airport police shoot him dead while a small boy watches from the concourse.
The carrier passes through the gate with the virus in his luggage, taking the seat next to one of the scientists sent back from the future.
S67: At a girls' day school, a mistress takes charge of a set of ten-year-olds and informs them that she is in her prime.
She teaches them about her dead fiance, about Italian painting and about her own opinions, in place of the syllabus.
She walks the set through the old part of the city and halts them in front of a queue of unemployed men.
The headmistress tries repeatedly to force her resignation and can find no grounds for it.
The art master, who has one arm, a wife and six children, kisses her in the art room.
She gives him up and takes the singing master as her lover instead.
She spends her weekends at the singing master's house on the coast with two of the girls attending as chaperones.
She decides that one particular girl shall become the art master's lover in her place.
The set's dull one, whom everybody blames for everything, leaves the school.
A different girl becomes the art master's lover, and discovers that every portrait he paints of any of them comes out looking like their teacher.
The mistress encourages a new girl to run away and fight in a foreign war.
The new girl is killed when her train is attacked, having gone to fight for the wrong side.
The singing master marries the science mistress.
The girl who became the art master's lover tells the headmistress that their teacher instructs in fascism, and hands her the grounds she has wanted for years.
The mistress is forced into retirement and spends her life trying to work out which of the set betrayed her.
The dull one dies at twenty-three in a hotel fire, running the wrong way along a corridor.
The mistress dies of an internal growth, and her betrayer, an enclosed nun who has written a book on psychology, is asked through the grille what the chief influences of her schooldays were.
S69: A sound truck for a fringe presidential candidate circles the city broadcasting his platform to nobody in particular.
An ageing country star records a patriotic anthem while a foreign reporter drifts round the studio talking into a tape recorder.
The city's best loved singer collapses at her own airport welcome and is taken to hospital.
A pile-up on the freeway strands most of the city's musicians and hangers-on together.
A gospel singer performs with her choir while her husband negotiates with the candidate's organiser.
A folk trio records together while the man among them sleeps with women from every other storyline.
A quiet young man arrives in the city with a violin case and takes a room from an old widower whose wife is dying.
A waitress who has walked out on her husband keeps trying to get onto any stage that will let her sing.
A girl with no voice at all performs at a men's smoker and is made to strip for the room.
The best loved singer is discharged from hospital and breaks down on stage, rambling at the audience until she is led away.
The country star refuses to appear at the candidate's rally unless his own conditions are met.
The gospel singer sleeps with the folk singer after his set and goes home to her deaf children.
The widower's wife dies on the ward, and the young man lodging with him never notices.
The organiser assembles the rally by promising every performer something different.
The best loved singer performs at the rally and is shot in front of the crowd by the young man with the violin case.
The country star, hit in the arm, tells the crowd that this is their city and passes the microphone to the waitress.
The waitress gets her stage and leads the crowd in a song while the ambulances pull away.
The crowd goes on singing as the camera withdraws over their heads.
S70: A doctor whose face was destroyed in the war sits in the lobby telling anyone passing that people come and go and nothing ever happens here.
A bookkeeper who has been told he is dying cashes in his savings and takes the most expensive room in the building.
A ruined nobleman working the corridors as a thief is pressed by his creditors for money he has not got.
A manufacturer arrives to close a merger that will collapse unless he lies about it.
A famous dancer refuses to go on, saying nobody comes to watch her.
The manufacturer engages a typist and makes clear what else the position involves.
The thief hides in the dancer's room to take her pearls and instead spends the night listening to her.
She discovers him there, and the two of them are in love.
The bookkeeper loses his temper in the bar with the manufacturer, who is his own employer, and tells him precisely what he thinks of him.
The thief takes up with the bookkeeper and teaches him to drink and to dance.
The dancer performs better than she has and arranges to leave for the south with the thief.
The bookkeeper wins heavily at cards and then loses his wallet, and the thief, who took it, hands it back.
The manufacturer's merger collapses when the truth about the foreign contract comes out.
The thief breaks into the manufacturer's room for the money, and the manufacturer beats him to death with a telephone.
The manufacturer is arrested, the dancer leaves for her train believing her lover will follow, the bookkeeper takes the typist away with him, and the doctor repeats that nothing ever happens.
S71: At an airport arrivals gate strangers greet the people they love, and a voice remarks that love is in fact everywhere.
A newly elected prime minister meets a young woman who works in the household at his official residence.
An ageing rocker records a festive version of an old hit and tells every interviewer it is rubbish.
A woman marries her fiance, and his closest friend films the whole wedding.
A widower buries his wife and cannot get his stepson to speak to him at all.
A writer finds his girlfriend in bed with his brother and goes abroad to work alone.
The head of a design agency finds that his new secretary is paying him a great deal of attention.
The agency head's wife runs a household around her daughter's part in a school nativity play.
A woman at the agency has loved a colleague and is interrupted every time by calls from her ill brother.
The stepson admits he is in love with a girl at school, and the widower is relieved that it is only that.
The writer and his foreign housekeeper fall in love without a word of shared language.
The friend shows the bride his wedding footage, which turns out to be entirely of her, and stands at her door with a stack of cue cards.
A visiting head of state makes a pass at the young woman, and the prime minister denounces him at the press conference.
The agency head buys his secretary a necklace, and his wife finds it, assumes it is for her, and is given a compact disc instead.
The woman from the agency takes her colleague home, and leaves the bed to answer her brother's call.
The rocker's record goes to number one and he spends the holiday with his manager rather than at a party.
The writer flies south and proposes in front of an entire street, the prime minister finds the young woman backstage at the nativity play, and the widower takes his stepson through airport security.
Everyone arrives at the same airport, and the telling closes on the gate it opened at.
S72: A career field officer sells two missiles in a Middle Eastern capital and loses track of one, which an arms dealer carries off.
In an oil-rich desert state the drilling rights held by a large western company are handed instead to a Chinese firm.
A migrant labourer on the state's oilfield is laid off along with his father when the contract changes hands.
The western company announces a merger with a small firm that has won drilling rights in central Asia.
A government inquiry opens into the merger, and a young lawyer is instructed to turn up exactly enough corruption to satisfy it.
An energy analyst brings his family to a party at the ruler's palace, where his small son is electrocuted in the swimming pool.
The ruler's elder son takes on the analyst as an adviser, out of guilt and out of conviction both.
The labourer and his father queue for work and are drawn into a school where a preacher takes a close interest in them.
The field officer is sent to arrange the killing of the elder son, who is judged unfriendly to western interests.
He is betrayed to a militia, tortured and dumped, and comes home to find his own service suspects him.
The elder son sets out his programme: the rights go to the highest bidder, the parliament gets real power, and women get the vote.
The lawyer establishes that an executive at the small firm paid bribes for the central Asian field, and delivers him to the inquiry along with his own mentor.
The ruler names his younger son rather than his elder as successor.
The field officer works out that the killing is going ahead regardless and drives into the desert to warn the prince.
The labourer and another young man take the missing missile out to sea in a fishing boat.
A missile from a drone destroys the prince's convoy in the desert, killing him, his family, the analyst's employer and the field officer.
The labourer steers the boat into the side of a new tanker and the missile detonates.
The merger goes through, and the men who engineered the whole of it are photographed collecting a prize.
S73: On the hottest morning of the year a disc jockey opens his broadcast from a storefront window on the block.
A young man gets out of bed at his sister's flat and goes off to deliver pizzas.
The pizzeria owner opens up with his two sons, the elder saying he hates the neighbourhood and everybody in it.
The block's old drunk buys his first beer of the day and is scolded for it by a woman watching from her window.
A regular objects that the photographs on the pizzeria wall are all of the owner's own countrymen and asks where the black faces are.
The owner throws him into the street, and he starts calling for a boycott that nobody joins.
A big quiet man walks the block with a boombox playing one song at full volume.
Three older men sit under an umbrella opposite a Korean grocery and talk about the block.
A stammering man works the corner selling hand-coloured photographs of two murdered leaders.
The delivery man tells the owner's elder son to his face that every one of his heroes is black.
The old drunk pulls a child out of the path of a car, and the woman at the window softens towards him.
The hydrant is opened and the whole block plays in the water until a police car pulls up.
The big man and the boycotter come into the pizzeria with the radio at full volume, demanding the wall be changed.
The owner smashes the boombox with a baseball bat and the fight spills into the street.
Police arrive and kill the big man with a chokehold in front of the entire block.
The delivery man throws a rubbish bin through the pizzeria window and the crowd burns the place down.
He comes back for his week's wages, and the two of them argue over the money among the ashes.
S74: Four young men say their prayers in a hotel room, and in the departure lounge before they board.
A regional traffic centre notices an aircraft has stopped answering and picks up a hijacker's voice on the frequency.
The national operations centre starts tracking the aircraft that has gone quiet.
The first aircraft hits the north tower, and the controllers watch it on a television without believing what they see.
Passengers for the fourth flight take their seats and wait out a long delay on the tarmac.
The military sector is ordered to scramble fighters and cannot be told where to send them.
The second aircraft hits the south tower on live television.
The national centre orders every aircraft in the country onto the ground at once.
The third aircraft hits the defence headquarters outside the capital.
The hijackers aboard the fourth aircraft kill the pilots, take the cockpit and turn back east.
Passengers get through to families and answering machines on the seat phones and piece together what has happened elsewhere.
The passengers agree among themselves that the aircraft will not be allowed to reach wherever it is pointed.
Fighters are launched, unarmed, with no clear authority to bring anything down.
The passengers charge up the aisle behind a drinks trolley and force their way towards the flight deck.
The man at the controls rolls the aircraft and puts it into a dive.
The aircraft comes down in open farmland.
S75: A boy is born in a small industrial town and grows into a weak, peculiar child.
His father throws him into the deep end of a pool to teach him to swim, and he sinks to the bottom.
He is conscripted as a chaplain's assistant and shipped overseas with no training worth the name.
He is lost behind the lines with a scout who beats him for wanting to be left to die.
The pair are captured, and the scout dies of gangrene on the prison train, blaming him with his last breath.
He is held in a camp beside enemy officers who have been drawing double rations through a clerical error.
He is sent on to a great city and housed with other prisoners in a disused abattoir.
The city is destroyed by fire, and the prisoners in the meat locker come up to find it gone.
The prisoners are made to dig bodies out of the cellars until one of the diggers dies of the dry heaves.
A fellow prisoner promises to have him killed on the dead scout's account.
He comes home, collapses, and is hospitalised, where another patient introduces him to a hack science fiction writer.
He marries the daughter of the man who owns the optometry school and becomes rich.
He survives an air crash in the mountains, and his wife dies of exhaust fumes driving to the hospital.
He is taken by aliens and kept in a zoo on their planet with a film actress.
The aliens explain that every moment exists at once and that free will is an idea peculiar to his own planet.
He goes on a radio talk show and tries to tell the world about the aliens and the fourth dimension.
His daughter decides he is senile and takes his affairs out of his hands.
He is shot dead by a beam weapon after addressing a crowd, exactly as he has always known he would be.
S77: A career thief serves nine years in prison abroad while his daughter grows up without him.
The daughter moves to the west coast and takes up with a wealthy record producer.
She works out that he is laundering drug money and threatens to go to the police.
His head of security kills her and dresses it as a crash on a canyon road.
The thief is released, reads a newspaper cutting somebody has posted to him, and flies out.
He finds an acquaintance of his daughter's, who tells him the little he knows.
He goes to a warehouse to ask questions, is beaten and thrown into the street, and walks back in and kills everyone in it.
He meets his daughter's acting teacher, who tells him exactly what sort of father he was.
He and the acquaintance watch the producer's house from the hills above it.
He gatecrashes a party at the house, and the security men drive him into the desert to shoot him.
He kills the men in the desert and walks back out to the road.
The producer runs to a beach house up the coast with his young girlfriend.
The two men drive north, and the acquaintance is shot dead in the assault on the beach house.
The thief corners the producer on the rocks, and the producer admits the girl died out of his own panic.
He lets the producer live, flies home, and thinks about a day at the seaside with his daughter as a small child.
S76: A bombardier arrives on the island base and flies his first missions.
A gunner is hit over a target town and dies in the bombardier's arms as he finds the second wound under the flak suit.
The colonel raises the number of missions required to go home, then raises it again, and again after that.
The bombardier reports sick with a liver complaint just short of jaundice and stays in hospital as long as the doctors permit.
He censors the enlisted men's letters out of boredom and signs them with a borrowed name.
An investigator arrives to look into the forged signatures and turns up nothing whatever.
The squadron doctor explains that asking to be grounded for madness proves sanity, and is therefore grounds for nothing.
The mess officer builds a syndicate trading across both sides of the front and corners an entire country's cotton crop.
The mess officer contracts with the enemy to bomb his own squadron for an agreed fee.
One unfailingly cheerful patient empties the ward of every other man in it.
A idealistic airman is tried for an offence nobody can name, and flies into a cloud and is never seen again.
The squadron doctor is recorded as dead because his name was on a flight manifest, and no paperwork can restore him.
A young airman falls in love with a prostitute who is asleep every time he calls on her.
The young airman is killed over a coastal target, and his prostitute blames the bombardier and tries to knife him wherever he goes.
The military police clear out the apartments, and the bombardier walks back through the city alone past one atrocity after another.
A fellow officer rapes and kills a maid and is not arrested, while the bombardier is arrested for being in the city without a pass.
The colonel and his second offer the bombardier a bargain: say the squadron is wonderful and go home a hero.
He refuses the bargain, learns that a lost comrade rowed all the way to neutral waters, and sets out to follow him.
S78: A boy with a stammer is treated by a hypnotist on television and speaks one clear sentence.
A young mother sits on a fence outside a country house waiting for a husband who never comes.
A doctor passing along the road stops to talk to her, and the fence collapses under the pair of them.
A barn burns while the family stand in the doorway and watch without moving.
The mother runs through the rain to the printing house certain she has let a fatal misprint through, and finds she has not.
The father comes home on leave during the war, and the children are shy of him.
The mother takes her son to sell her earrings to a doctor's wife in a warm house, and cannot make herself do it.
At a training camp a boy who has lost his entire family refuses an order and lies down on a grenade.
The grown son's own small boy, alone in the flat, reads a letter aloud to a woman who is not there.
The son quarrels with his former wife down the telephone about their child.
He watches his mother cross a field with two children.
He lies ill in a darkened room while the doctors agree there is nothing physically wrong with him.
He remembers a girl at school with a cracked lip whom he could never bring himself to speak to.
A gust of wind crosses a field of buckwheat towards the house, and nobody indoors remarks on it.
An elderly woman walks two children over a meadow in the failing light as the camera draws back among the trees.
S79: A young woman is taught by nuns that there are two ways through a life, the way of nature and the way of grace.
She marries, and their first son is born.
Two more sons follow, and the three boys run wild through a small southern town.
Their father drills them in discipline at the dinner table and teaches the middle one the guitar.
Their mother plays with them on the lawn while the father is away on business.
The eldest, jealous and confused, breaks a neighbour's window and steals a slip from a woman's drawer.
The eldest takes his brother into the yard, persuades him to put a finger over an air rifle, and shoots him.
The father loses his job when the plant closes and the family have to give up the house.
The eldest asks his brother's forgiveness in a doorway without managing to say any of the words.
A telegram reports that the middle brother has died at nineteen, and the mother cannot be consoled.
The father tells his eldest that he was too hard on all of them.
Galaxies condense, stars burn out, a planet cools, and something first stirs in its oceans.
A wounded creature lies in a river bed while another sets a foot on its head and then lets it live.
The eldest, a middle-aged architect in a glass tower, cannot get through the anniversary of his brother's death.
He walks through a doorway standing alone in a desert and finds everyone he has lost gathered on a shore.
S80: A conscript soldier lands on the coast with an armoured column.
His unit fires at a car approaching a roadblock and finds a family inside it.
A comrade swims out to sea from a burning landing craft and lives when the rest of his unit does not.
Another soldier dances with a machine gun down a boulevard under sniper fire, beneath posters of an assassinated leader.
The unit shells an orchard and a boy carrying a rocket launcher is killed in front of them.
The soldier and two others bathe in the sea under flares while the city burns behind them.
Armed irregulars go into the refugee camps while the soldiers outside send up flares to light the sky for them.
The militia kill the people in the camps, while the soldiers on the roofs fail to grasp what they are watching.
The soldier stands at the edge of the camp as the women come out screaming.
A friend tells him over a drink about a recurring dream of twenty-six dogs.
He realises he remembers nothing whatever of the war and sets out to find the men he served with.
A psychologist explains to him that memory can be assembled out of what a person needs rather than what occurred.
A television reporter tells him what he saw in the camps and what he said to the defence minister on the telephone.
He understands that the flare-lit memory of himself in the sea is a screen he built to stand between himself and the camps.
S81: A girl is brought to a farm in the border states and chooses one of the men there for herself.
The man's mother is bought out of slavery by his extra labour and settles in a house outside a northern city.
A new owner the slaves nickname after his schooling arrives and starts measuring them and writing them up in a ledger.
The young woman overhears him instructing his nephews to list her animal characteristics on one side of the page and her human ones on the other.
The men at the farm lay a plan to run for it, and the plan falls apart.
The nephews hold her down in the barn and take her milk while her husband watches from the loft and loses his reason.
Pregnant and beaten, she walks north alone, and a white girl delivers her baby in a beached boat.
She reaches the house and has twenty-eight days of freedom, and her mother-in-law holds a feast for ninety people.
The owner comes to the house to take her and the children back.
She carries the children into the woodshed and cuts her elder daughter's throat with a handsaw.
She is jailed and released, her mother-in-law takes to her bed and dies, and the neighbours stop calling.
Her two sons run away from a house haunted by the dead baby.
One of the men from the farm arrives and drives the ghost out of the house.
A young woman walks out of the water, gives the dead child's name as her own, and comes to live with them.
The man is moved out of the house room by room and is taken to bed by the visitor in the shed.
An old friend shows him the newspaper cutting about the killing, and he leaves.
The visitor swells and consumes the mother, until thirty women come into the yard and sing until she is gone.
S83: A man meets a woman at a party and the two of them begin living together.
She is cold and low and keeps the heating up in a flat he finds airless.
The pair take a holiday in the north, where she is happier.
He has an affair with a colleague and says nothing whatever about it to her.
She dies of gas in the flat while he is out walking.
The police question him, conclude it was an accident, and he says nothing about the tap.
He tries to shoot himself and only wounds himself.
He spends time in hospital and comes out with nothing to do and nobody expecting him.
Two researchers stop him at the hospital gates and ask him to be their first human subject, on the grounds that a man indifferent to whether he lives is exactly what they want.
He is driven to a laboratory in the country and shown a machine shaped like an enormous soft brain.
He is sealed inside it with a mouse and sent back exactly one year for exactly one minute, to swim in the sea.
The machine misfires, and he starts reliving fragments of his life in no order at all, the same seconds again and again.
The researchers lose control of the machine, cannot retrieve him, and search the grounds.
He is found on the lawn outside the laboratory, shot through the chest by his own hand, and dies.
S82: In a border town a married mother of four meets a farmer and the two begin an affair in a trailer out in the fields.
Her eldest daughter discovers the affair and follows her mother out to the trailer.
A gas leak sets the trailer burning and both the woman and the farmer die in it.
The daughter is left to bring up her younger sisters while her father drinks and blames himself.
The farmer's son comes to the town to look at the wreck and to find out who the woman was.
The two children of the dead recognise each other and, out of grief more than anything else, become lovers.
The girl burns down her own family's house with her father's photographs inside it.
She finds she is pregnant, and the two of them run away together.
The boy is badly injured when their car leaves the road, and she is told he has died.
She gives birth to a daughter, leaves the baby with the boy's family, and vanishes.
Under another name she runs a restaurant on the northern coast, sleeps with men she does not know, and cuts herself.
The boy, alive and badly scarred, works as a crop duster with his own small daughter beside him.
He crashes his aircraft, and the child is brought north by a friend to look for her mother.
The friend finds the restaurant owner and tells her that the boy is alive and that her daughter is with him.
She flies south, and mother and daughter meet in a hospital corridor.
S25: Supermarket checkout girl Corey takes Marek's shift because he is driving to the desert casino city and she is about to be evicted.
A narcotics detective named Kessel catches the soap actors Reid and Vaughn buying and puts them in wires to make a case against their dealer.
Reid and Vaughn come to Marek's till asking for twenty hits of ecstasy.
Corey takes the deal herself and goes with her friend Bett to Marek's dealer, Nyle.
Nyle refuses to front the drugs, so Corey leaves Bett in his flat as collateral and takes the pills on credit.
In the car park Corey spots Kessel waiting with Reid and Vaughn and realises the buy is a sting.
Corey flushes the ecstasy and sells the pair crushed cold remedies instead.
Marek and his friend Ozzie talk their way into a free suite, a wedding chapel and a strip club.
Marek sleeps with two women and leaves a hotel room on fire.
Kessel takes Reid and Vaughn home to dinner, where his real interest turns out to be signing them into a pyramid scheme with his wife Deb.
Corey goes to a warehouse rave to unload the rest of the aspirin on strangers.
Marek takes a security guard's gun in the club, shoots the bouncer through the arm, and the four run for the car.
The club's owner chases them out into the desert and shoots the borrowed sports car to pieces.
Nyle works out that he has been cheated and comes after Corey at the rave, and she runs out into the road.
Reid and Vaughn, driving home, are the ones who hit her, and they panic and leave her in an alley.
Marek gets back to town and Nyle corners him over the money, and Marek shoots Nyle through the arm.
Corey comes round in the alley and reaches the diner, where all three stories meet.
S62: Four sisters put on the eldest girl's play in the attic and carry their own breakfast down the road to a starving family.
The writer of the play meets the boy next door at a dance while hiding a scorch mark in the back of her dress.
The youngest sister is caned in front of her class over a jar of sweets and is withdrawn from the school.
The youngest burns her sister's manuscript, and is told she will never be forgiven.
The youngest goes through the ice on the river, and the sister who nearly let her drown forgives her.
The shy sister is given a dead child's piano by the old man next door.
A telegram reports their father wounded, and the eldest sells her hair to pay for their mother's journey to him.
The shy sister catches scarlet fever from the family they have been feeding and very nearly dies.
The second sister marries a poor tutor in the garden with almost no money and is glad of it.
The boy next door proposes and is refused, on the grounds that the two of them would destroy each other.
The writer sells lurid stories to a city paper under an invented name while a foreign professor at her lodging house tells her frankly that they are bad.
The youngest studies painting abroad under a rich aunt's eye and meets the boy next door, drunk and aimless.
The married sister, poor, buys dress silk she cannot afford and confesses it to her husband.
Word arrives that the shy sister is dying, and the writer goes home to nurse her beside the sea.
The shy sister dies, and the writer shuts herself in the attic and starts writing the story of the four of them.
The youngest and the boy next door marry abroad and come home together, and a letter offering herself to him arrives too late.
The writer argues the ending and the copyright out of her publisher, and the book goes to press.
S64: A screenwriter behind on his payments is dodging the finance men who have come for his car.
He pitches a baseball picture at a studio and a script reader tells the producer to his face that it is flat.
Fleeing the finance men, he blows a tyre and swings into the drive of a crumbling mansion on a famous boulevard.
Mistaken for the undertaker come to collect a dead chimpanzee, he meets a silent-era star nobody has thought about.
She hires him to cut down the enormous script she has written as a vehicle for herself.
He moves into the room over the garage, and her butler fetches his belongings from his flat without being asked.
She buys him suits, a cigarette case and a watch, and the arrangement quietly becomes a kept one.
At a party laid on for two she tells him she loves him, and he walks out to a friend's party instead.
The butler telephones to say she has opened her wrists, and he comes back and stays.
He starts slipping out to write a script with the reader, who is engaged to a friend of his.
She drives to the studio with her script; a famous director is gentle with her, and the writer learns the studio only ever wanted to rent her car.
The butler admits that he directed her first pictures, that he was her first husband, and that he has been writing her fan letters himself.
She telephones the reader, and he brings the girl to the house and tells her exactly what he is, so that she will go.
He packs, tells the old star the truth about her career and the letters, and walks out towards the pool.
She shoots him three times and he falls face down into the swimming pool.
With the police and the newsreel cameras filling the hall, she takes them for a film crew and descends the staircase ready for her close-up.
S14: Nolan sees Wren for the first time when she is introduced as the boss's new assistant at the greeting-card company.
Wren overhears Nolan playing a band he loves in the lift and tells him she loves them too.
at a company karaoke night Wren sings, and Nolan's friend Dev drunkenly tells her that Nolan likes her.
Wren kisses Nolan in the office copy room.
Wren tells Nolan she does not believe in love and wants nothing serious.
they sleep together, and Nolan dances through the street to work.
Nolan and Wren play house through a furniture showroom and are perfectly happy.
Wren shows Nolan her bedroom and tells him things she says she has never told anyone.
Nolan punches a man in a bar for hitting on Wren, and Wren is furious with him for it.
a distance has opened between them, and Wren cries at the end of an old film about an interrupted wedding.
Wren ends the relationship over pancakes in a diner.
Nolan falls apart at work, drinks through the day and writes a bitter greeting card that gets him hauled in front of his boss.
Nolan quits the card company to go back to architecture.
at a colleague's wedding Wren catches the bouquet, and she and Nolan dance and talk warmly.
Nolan goes to Wren's party expecting a reconciliation and finds an engagement ring on her finger, with the screen splitting his expectations from what actually happens.
Nolan shuts himself in, then his sister Elsie and his own drawings pull him back towards architecture.
Wren, married, finds Nolan on their bench and tells him she simply became certain with someone else.
Nolan meets another candidate, Lark, at a job interview and asks her out, and the counter resets.
S17: Child psychologist Aubrey Lang and his wife Frida celebrate a civic award for his work with children.
A former patient named Emory breaks into their bathroom, accuses Aubrey of having failed him, shoots him in the stomach and then kills himself.
Aubrey bleeds to death on the bedroom floor with Frida beside him.
Aubrey takes on nine-year-old Toby Salter, a withdrawn boy whose case reminds him of Emory's.
Toby's mother Dana keeps finding cupboards standing open, drawers pulled out and marks on her son's body that she cannot explain.
Toby is shut in a cupboard at a birthday party and comes out hysterical and bruised.
Aubrey arrives late for his wedding anniversary dinner and Frida leaves the restaurant without speaking to him.
Toby tells Aubrey that he sees dead people walking around who do not know that they are dead.
Aubrey almost drops the case, then replays the tape of Emory and hears a terrified voice in another language behind his own.
Aubrey tells Toby to stop running from the ghosts and to listen to what they want from him.
Bree Marlow, a girl who has died, appears in Toby's tent and hands him a videotape.
At Bree's wake Toby gives her father the tape, which shows her stepmother poisoning her food.
Toby tells his mother about the ghosts and repeats what his dead grandmother heard her say at the graveside, and Dana believes him.
No longer terrified, Toby is cast in the school play and is happy in it.
Aubrey tells Toby that he has helped him and that the two of them will not need to see each other again.
Aubrey goes home, watches his and Frida's wedding video, and sees that she is asleep and has been talking to no one.
Frida's hand opens and Aubrey's wedding ring falls out, and he finds the bullet wound in his own back.
Aubrey tells his sleeping wife that he loves her and lets go.
S23: The blind clockmaker Ferrier builds a station clock that runs backwards, in memory of the son it took from him.
The manufacturer Ellis Wray's wife dies in childbirth and he abandons the baby - an infant with the body of an old man - on the steps of a nursing home.
Odessa, who runs the home, takes Amos in and raises him among the elderly residents.
Amos, apparently in his eighties, gets out of his wheelchair and walks.
Amos meets six-year-old Clara, the granddaughter of a resident, and the two become inseparable.
Amos takes work on a tugboat skippered by a man called Rook and leaves the river city.
Wintering in a northern port, Amos has an affair with Eleanor Trask, the wife of a trade official.
The tug is drafted into the war and Rook and most of the crew are killed ramming a submarine.
Amos comes home, and Ellis Wray reveals himself as his father and leaves him the fastener factory.
Clara, a dancer in the capital, visits, and Amos turns her down as too young for him.
Clara's leg is shattered by a car abroad and she refuses Amos's help.
Her dancing over, Clara comes back to the river city, and she and Amos meet in the middle of their lives.
Odessa dies, and Amos and Clara sell up and live together on a boat and then in a house of their own.
Their daughter Josie is born, and Amos, visibly younger every year, decides she cannot have a father who will become her brother.
Amos signs everything over to Clara and leaves.
Clara marries again and raises Josie, while Amos travels the world alone and sends postcards.
Amos comes back, in his twenties, and spends a night with Clara before leaving again.
Clara is called to collect a boy found in a derelict building with Amos's diary, and cares for him as he forgets everything.
Amos dies in Clara's arms as an infant.
With a hurricane bearing down on the coast, Josie finishes reading the diary to her dying mother and learns who her father was, while the backwards clock sits in a flooding storage room.
S18: The lawyer Josiah Vane, crossing an ocean homeward, watches the slave trade at work while the ship's doctor Mowbray quietly poisons him for his gold.
The stowaway Kesa, whose life Josiah saved, nurses him through the poisoning and exposes Mowbray.
Josiah reaches port and renounces his father-in-law's slaving fortune to join the abolitionists.
The penniless composer Rafe Sorrell talks his way into the household of the ailing Delacroix as his amanuensis, writing constantly to his lover Merrick.
Rafe finds half of Josiah's journal in the estate library and writes the Skywater Suite while Delacroix tries to claim it as his own.
Rafe finishes the Suite, shoots himself in a hotel bath in an old town, and Merrick arrives too late.
The journalist Nia Sol is trapped in a stalled lift with the elderly Merrick, who tells her about a suppressed safety report on the Havenrock plant.
Merrick is murdered, Nia inherits Rafe's letters to him, and a hitman called Vole runs her car off a bridge.
Nia and the engineer Behr's report bring the conspiracy down and she publishes the story.
The publisher Aldous Prynne, hunted by an author's gangster brothers, is tricked by his own brother into signing himself into the Bellmont nursing home.
Drugged and locked in, Aldous reads Nia's manuscript and organises an escape with three fellow residents.
The escapees fight their way out through a crowded pub, and Aldous writes his ordeal up as a screenplay.
The fabricant server Sena-19 is lifted out of a diner chain by the rebel Jun and shown what the world outside is.
Sena watches the film of Aldous's escape, learns that spent fabricants are recycled into food for the living, and records a declaration of her rights.
Sena is captured and executed, and her declaration survives her as scripture.
The goatherd Odo, whose tribe worships Sena as a god, guides the technologically advanced traveller Sarai up to a mountain observatory while the Rakka raid his valley.
Odo ignores the whispering demon Tallow, kills a Rakka warrior, and Sarai sends the signal that will bring a ship.
Off world, Odo tells his grandchildren the whole story under an alien sky, with Sarai beside him.
S05: In a mining boarding house out west, Emmett Rusk's mother signs her son over to the banker Barrow after a defaulted lodger's mine deed makes the family rich.
The boy drives his sled into Barrow's stomach and is taken east away from his parents anyway.
Emmett takes control of the fortune and tells Barrow that of all his holdings he wants to run a failing city newspaper, the Clarion.
Emmett moves into the Clarion, installs his manager Marsh and his friend Devlin, and prints a signed statement of principles on the front page.
Emmett hires away the entire staff of the rival paper and throws a party with a brass band and a chorus line.
Emmett returns from a buying trip abroad engaged to Adele, the governor's niece.
A run of breakfast-table scenes charts the marriage cooling into silence behind separate newspapers.
Emmett meets the shopgirl Nora Kell on the street with mud on his coat and starts visiting her rooms in secret.
During the campaign for governor, the party boss Halloran brings Adele to Nora's rooms and threatens exposure, and Emmett refuses to withdraw.
Emmett loses the election, Devlin asks to be transferred to another city, and the marriage collapses.
Emmett marries Nora and forces her into an opera career for which she has no voice.
Nora's debut is a humiliation, and a drunk Devlin begins the savage review that Emmett finishes, prints, and fires him for.
Nora swallows poison rather than sing again, and Emmett lets her stop.
Emmett shuts Nora away in the half-finished palace he calls Silvermount, where she works jigsaw puzzles in the vast empty hall.
After a joyless beach picnic and a quarrel, Nora packs and leaves him.
Emmett wrecks Nora's bedroom, finds a glass snow globe, murmurs "Bluebell", and carries it past the endless mirrors.
Alone at Silvermount, Emmett dies with the word "Bluebell" on his lips and drops the snow globe on the floor.
A newsreel obituary recaps Emmett's public life and closes without explaining his last word.
The reporter Nash is sent to find out what "Bluebell" means and is turned away by a drunk Nora in a seaside nightclub.
Nash reads Barrow's memoir and interviews Marsh, Devlin, Nora and the butler Colm before concluding that no single word explains a life, as workmen shovel a sled marked Bluebell into the furnace.
S30: The old woman Ottilie Crane tells Theo that every living creature on this earth dies alone.
Theo Lund is woken by a voice and sleepwalks out of the house onto a golf course.
A jet engine falls out of nowhere and destroys Theo's bedroom while he is outside.
In the restored timeline Theo stays in his bed laughing, and is killed when the engine comes through the roof.
Theo wakes on the green with a countdown of days, hours, minutes and seconds written on his arm by a figure in a hare costume who calls himself Vex.
The household is relocated while the roof is rebuilt, and no authority can account for where the engine came from.
Vex tells Theo the world will end.
Theo meets Marin Alder, a new girl seated next to him in a literature class, and asks her out.
On Vex's instruction Theo puts an axe through a water main to flood the school and buries the axe in the bronze mascot.
Theo's therapist Dr. Belding raises his medication and puts him under hypnosis.
The science teacher Nadeau lends Theo the old woman's book, The Shape of Hours.
Theo starts seeing liquid spears coming out of people's chests and leading them where they are going.
Theo humiliates the motivational speaker Vaughn Tice in front of the whole school, and the teacher Miss Hobbs is sacked over her syllabus.
Tice is exposed as the owner of a child pornography ring after Theo burns his house down.
Theo and Marin sleep together during a costume party while his parents are away.
Theo takes Marin to find Ottilie Crane, and the bullies Cutch and Ryle attack them at her house.
A car driven by Vex in his hare costume runs Marin down and kills her.
Theo shoots Vex through the eye with his father's revolver.
Theo carries Marin's body up the hill and watches a vortex open over his house.
Theo sends the jet engine back through the vortex, closing the tangent universe, and Marin cycles past the house not knowing who died there.
S35: Thirteen-year-old Junia Thorne finishes a play to be performed for her brother's homecoming.
Junia watches from an upstairs window as her sister Rosalind strips to her underwear and climbs into the fountain in front of Tom Vasey, the housekeeper's son.
Tom drafts a letter of apology to Rosalind, sends the obscene version by mistake, and Junia reads it on the way.
Junia walks in on Tom and Rosalind making love in the library and takes it for an assault.
The twins run off, and during the search Junia sees their cousin Cissy being raped in the dark and names Tom as the man.
Tom is arrested and taken away in front of the family, and Rosalind breaks with all of them.
Tom is released from prison into the army and is separated from his unit in the retreat across the continent.
Rosalind, a nurse in the city, writes to Tom, and the two spend a few hours together on his leave.
Tom walks to the evacuation beach with two corporals and reaches a shore of burning vehicles, shot horses and thousands of waiting men.
Tom lies down in a cinema on the seafront and dies of septicaemia before the ships come.
Junia, eighteen, takes a nursing place in the city instead of the university place she was offered, and treats men brought back from the continent.
Junia learns that Cissy is marrying Neville Frome, the man who actually raped her.
Junia goes to Rosalind's flat, finds Tom there, and promises to recant her statement and set the truth down in writing.
Rosalind is killed when a bomb bursts the water main above an underground station.
The elderly Junia, dying and giving her last interview, admits that she never went to the flat and that Tom and Rosalind never saw each other again.
Junia says she gave the two of them in her novel the life they were never allowed, and the film shows them together at a seaside cottage.
S34: In a suburb outside the city, the novelist Vera Holt begins writing The Hostess while her husband Edmund and the servants manage her illness.
Vera's sister Nell visits with her children, and a dying bird is buried in the garden.
Vera tells Edmund at the railway station that she will die if she is kept in the suburb, and he agrees to move back to the city.
Vera decides that her heroine will live and that someone else - a poet - will die instead.
Vera fills her coat pockets with stones and walks into the river, leaving a letter for Edmund.
The pregnant housewife Hazel Fenn reads The Hostess in bed rather than get up for her husband Walter's birthday.
Hazel and her small son Robin fail at making a birthday cake and start it again from scratch.
Hazel's neighbour June comes to ask her to feed the dog while she goes into hospital, and Hazel kisses her.
Hazel leaves Robin with a sitter, takes a hotel room and lays out sleeping pills, and then decides to live.
Hazel comes home, gets through the birthday dinner, and leaves her family for good once the second baby is born.
Miriam Crest buys flowers for a party for her friend Gideon, a poet dying of an incurable illness who calls her by the name of the novel's heroine.
Miriam argues with Gideon, who will not be consoled and wants neither the party nor the prize.
Gideon's former lover Ansel visits, and Miriam breaks down in her kitchen over the summer they were all happy.
Miriam's daughter Fern and her partner Marnie watch her hold the whole day together.
Gideon tells Miriam he stayed alive for her, and lets go of the window ledge.
Hazel Fenn arrives from overseas for the wake and tells Miriam what she did and why.
Miriam lets Hazel stay the night, and Fern takes her upstairs.
Vera's letter to Edmund is read over all three women: to look life in the face, and to put it away.
S31: Time travel exists, is outlawed, and is used only by syndicates to send victims back to closers waiting in prairie cornfields.
Wilder kills the hooded men sent to him, collects his silver, takes eyedrop narcotics and banks half his pay for a new life in the old capital.
Wilder's handler Sarn tells him to learn the eastern language and go east instead.
Wilder's friend Roan lets his own older self run, and Sarn's men carve messages into young Roan until the old one is drawn back and killed.
Wilder gives up Roan's hiding place to Sarn to get his silver back.
Wilder's older self arrives in the cornfield without a hood, knocks him out and escapes, leaving the loop unclosed.
Wilder survives the east, becomes an enforcer, meets a woman and gives up the drugs for her.
The Reaper's men come for Wilder, kill his wife in the raid, and send him back to be closed.
Sarn's men take Wilder's silver and hunt both versions of him across the city.
The older Wilder wipes out a squad of gunmen in a diner ambush and tells his younger self he means to kill the child who will grow up to be the Reaper.
Wilder takes the map of three candidate children and drives out to the prairie farm of Tessa and her son Nim.
Nim, a telekinetic child, kills a farmhand in a rage, and Tessa admits she is his mother and left him.
The older Wilder hunts down and kills the first two children on his list.
The enforcer Skid and Sarn's men trace Wilder to the farm and are torn apart by Nim.
The older Wilder reaches the farm to kill Nim and shoots Tessa instead.
Wilder sees that Nim will become the Reaper if he watches his mother die, and shoots himself in the chest, erasing his older self.
Tessa lives, and holds her son in the road.
S36: On the tenement streets, Nix and his friends Pilo, Squint and Nino run errands and petty rackets for the local boss Sallo.
Duke arrives in the neighbourhood, and after fighting each other the two boys join forces.
Nix watches Dinah dance alone through a peephole in the back of her father's delicatessen.
The boys begin rolling drunks and stash the proceeds in a case inside a station locker.
Sallo shoots Nino dead in the street, Nix knifes Sallo in return, and Nix is sent to prison.
Released, Nix finds Duke running a large bootlegging operation with Pilo and Squint.
The gang work for the union man Corrigan and the crooked police chief Vasari, whose newborn son they swap in the maternity ward.
Nix hires a deserted seafront restaurant for Dinah, and rapes her in the car when she tells him she is leaving for the film capital.
The dry years end, and Duke, unwilling to stop, proposes robbing the federal bank.
Ruby and Nix agree that the only way to save Duke from himself is to have him arrested on a smaller job.
Nix telephones the police to tip them off, and is told at the scene that Duke, Pilo and Squint were shot dead and their bodies burned in the street.
Nix goes to the station locker for the gang's money, finds the suitcase empty, and leaves the city under another name.
In an opium den, Nix lies back and smiles at the ceiling.
Nix receives an invitation to the reinterment of his three friends in a mausoleum he never paid for.
Nix comes back to the city, finds Bunny behind the delicatessen counter, and is given the key to the same locker.
Nix finds the mausoleum with his own name on the plaque and a suitcase of money inside, described as an advance on his next job.
Nix visits Ruby at a retirement home endowed by Marrick, and she tells him Duke had wanted to die.
Nix finds Dinah backstage, the cabinet minister Marrick's mistress, and she tries to send him away without letting him see her son.
Nix goes to Marrick's house and finds Duke alive, having stolen everything, asking Nix to kill him.
Nix refuses to recognise him and walks away, and a garbage truck grinds past behind him as Duke disappears.
S44: Kes phones Mira in a panic: he has left eighty thousand in a bag on the train and has to hand it to his boss Vart.
Mira runs out of the flat past her mother on the telephone and down the stairwell past a woman with a pram and a growling dog.
Mira reaches her father's bank and finds him with his mistress Elke, who has told him she is pregnant.
Her father denies her the money, tells her he is not her father at all, and has her put out of the building.
Mira arrives too late; Kes has robbed a supermarket, and in the getaway a policeman shoots Mira dead.
In the second attempt Mira is tripped on the stairs and reaches the bank a moment later.
Her father, mid-argument with Elke, slaps her, and Mira takes the security guard's gun and robs the bank herself.
Mira gets out with the money and finds Kes, who is run over by an ambulance in front of her.
In the third attempt Mira is a moment earlier on the stairs and misses her father entirely, seeing him drive away with his colleague Vogl.
Mira walks into a casino, buys a single chip, and screams the roulette ball onto the same number twice to win far more than she needs.
Kes spots the tramp who took his bag and chases him down on foot.
Kes gets the money back at gunpoint and hands it to Vart with seconds to spare.
Mira arrives carrying a bag of her own, and Kes asks what is in it.
Mira and Kes lie in bed in red light asking each other whether the other really loves them.
Each attempt rewrites the futures of the strangers Mira passes - the woman with the pram, an office worker called Hanne, a cyclist - shown in bursts of snapshots.
Her father's fate diverges every time: publicly exposed, robbed by his own daughter, or killed in a crash with Vogl.
S38: Ingrid Ravn disappeared from the family island during a parade, on a day when a crash had blocked the only bridge.
Gustav Ravn has received a pressed flower on his birthday, which he takes as taunting from her killer.
Journalist Anders Sten loses a libel case against the financier Kolberg and resigns from his magazine.
Sonja Vik, a ward of the state and a researcher for a security firm, is handed a new guardian, Rask, after her old one has a stroke.
Sonja compiles the background report on Sten that persuades Gustav Ravn to hire him.
Gustav brings Sten out to the island to write a family history and, in truth, to find out who killed Ingrid.
Rask makes Sonja perform oral sex before he will release her own money.
Rask rapes Sonja at his flat, not knowing she has hidden a camera in her bag.
Sonja comes back, tasers Rask, marks him permanently as a rapist and blackmails him with the recording.
Sten works through the family archive, is shot at in the woods, and finds Ingrid's notebook full of names and numbers.
Sten's daughter Maja points out that the numbers are scripture verses.
Sten asks the security firm for a research assistant and is given Sonja, who has been reading his hard drive.
Together they match the verses to a series of ritual murders of women across the country.
They trace the killings to Otto Ravn, Ingrid's father, and then to her brother Viktor.
Viktor catches Sten, chains him in a soundproofed basement and explains what he does down there.
Sonja arrives, splits Viktor's face with a golf club, and lets him drive away to his death in a crash.
Sonja nurses Sten back to health and the two become lovers.
A cousin called Karin, living overseas, turns out to be Ingrid herself, using the cousin's name since fleeing her father and brother.
Ingrid comes home to Gustav, and Sten has his story.
Sonja, in disguise, empties Kolberg's accounts at a foreign bank and feeds Sten the story that destroys him, then sees him with his editor Britt and throws away the present she had bought.
S41: Meilin defies her father Renjie to emigrate overseas with Bao.
Meilin and Bao open a laundromat, and every other life she might have had closes off one by one.
Their daughter Junie grows up feeling judged, and Meilin cannot bring herself to accept her girlfriend Robin.
On the origin branch, a version of Meilin invents branch-jumping and pushes her own daughter's mind across every universe at once until it shatters, making the entity Kavra Nul.
Kavra Nul builds a black ring, a hole made of everything that ever mattered, and starts hunting for the Meilin who can face her.
In the laundromat, Meilin prepares for a tax audit while Bao tries and fails to hand her divorce papers.
Renjie arrives from overseas for the new year party, and Meilin hides Robin from him.
In the lift to the tax office, the origin-branch Bao takes over her husband's body and gives Meilin an earpiece and a set of instructions.
Meilin branch-jumps in a supply closet and fights the security guards with skills borrowed from a film-star version of herself.
The auditor Beulah Sneed turns berserk, and the tax office becomes a battlefield.
Meilin is shown the origin branch and told that Kavra Nul is her own daughter.
Meilin jumps through lives she never lived - film star, opera singer, teppanyaki chef, a world where people have hot dogs for fingers, two rocks on a cliff.
The origin-branch Bao is killed, and Meilin's mind begins to come apart as she jumps too far.
Meilin confronts Kavra Nul, who says she does not want to kill her but wants her to see that nothing matters.
Believing nothing matters, Meilin turns on the people around her and nearly follows her daughter into the ring.
Bao, in every universe at once, asks her to be kind, and Meilin starts fighting with kindness instead.
Meilin gives each attacker what they actually need, wins Renjie's acceptance of Robin, and reaches Junie at the edge of the ring.
Meilin tells Junie that even if nothing matters she would still choose to be here with her, and pulls her back.
Back at the tax office the family files the return together, and Meilin's attention drifts across every universe at once.
S48: Newsreel footage lays out the head of state's time in office, a failed invasion and a missile standoff.
The head of state is shot dead in a plaza in a southern city.
A patrolman is shot dead nearby, and Dale Kerrigan is arrested in a cinema and charged with both killings.
Kerrigan denies everything, calls himself a patsy, and is shot by a club owner named Sy Poulos in the basement of police headquarters.
River-city district attorney Hollis Trent notices Kerrigan's local connections and interviews the pilot Duvall.
Federal agents take the case away from Trent, and he lets it go.
The official commission publishes its single-bullet conclusion and twenty-six volumes of supporting evidence.
Trent reads the commission's report, finds it unbelievable, and reopens the investigation with his own staff.
Trent's team retrace Kerrigan's time in the river city, his leafleting for a pro-regime committee and his links to the investigator Bannon's office above a coffee warehouse.
Witnesses describe shots from a grassy rise, men flashing badges behind a fence, and a rifle in a window.
Duvall, terrified and drinking, tells Trent he is a dead man, and is found dead.
A prisoner named Delmar describes a party at which a man called Vasse, Duvall and Kerrigan discussed killing the head of state.
Trent meets a man in the capital who gives his name only as a letter, and who describes how the security detail was stripped, who stood to gain, and how such an operation would be run.
Trent charges the businessman Emile Vasse with conspiracy, identifying him as the man Delmar named.
The press turns on Trent, his staff resign, his marriage nearly collapses, and his witnesses die or recant.
At trial Trent runs an amateur film of the shooting over and over and argues the physical impossibility of the single-bullet theory.
Trent delivers a closing address to the jury about a coup and about telling the truth.
The jury acquits Vasse in under an hour while accepting that there was a conspiracy.
Closing captions record that Vasse's intelligence connection emerged, and that files remain sealed.
S49: Rory, a removals man with no plans beyond the day, moves an old man into a nursing home and hangs his photographs for him.
In the same home Rory catches sight of Mara visiting her grandmother, and takes her number out of the sign-in book.
Mara, a pre-med student, is sleeping with the wrestler Vic and living with parents who despise each other.
Rory and Mara meet on a bus, and she agrees to a night out.
Mara tap-dances on a shop-front step while Rory plays ukulele and sings a love song.
Vic beats Rory bloody in the street when he finds out about them.
Mara learns she is pregnant by Vic and books a termination.
Mara changes her mind on the table and walks out, and Rory tells her he will raise the child with her.
Rory and Mara marry at a courthouse with her grandmother and a few friends.
Mara is a nurse, Rory paints houses and drinks from the morning, and their daughter Poppy is five.
The family dog gets out through a gate Mara left open and is killed on the road.
Rory books a night in a cheap themed motel to force the marriage back to life.
Mara's employer offers her a better job at another practice, and Rory takes it badly.
At the motel they drink, fail to reach each other, and Rory pushes for sex Mara does not want.
Mara leaves to answer a call from work, Rory follows her drunk and makes a scene at the practice, and she is fired.
In the car park Mara tells Rory she has nothing left, and he demands to be told how to fix it.
They go back to Mara's father's house, and Rory forces the confrontation in front of Poppy.
Mara tells Rory it is over, and Poppy runs down the street after him begging him not to go.
Rory walks away into the fireworks as Poppy is carried back.
